resolution.correction: On synchronize, validate the event after SHA against the current PR head and classify the verified checkout. Continue validating the format of a supplied preview SHA and preserve the existing equality check on other actions.
resolution.prevention: A Git fixture advances the topic and builds fresh test merges. It covers both records and executable updates with a previous preview and rejects contradictory after, ref, checkout, parent or malformed preview identities. A replay of the actual hosted checkout yielded change_requires_full with its base and 24 changed paths.

items.source: Main push 45033552903 native Windows diagnostic at archives/runs/20261122T143714.976297Z-71b18a36/test-report.json.
items.observation: The removal committed revision 2. A BUSY probe was attributed to the intended holder, but that holder and the first browser snapshot both received 429. A later browser read and the persisted state confirmed revision 2 and a single removal.

resolution.cause: The test interpreted any HTTP 429 returned by an unrelated admission probe as evidence that its intended snapshot held the writer. A controlled competitor demonstrated the same 429 while the intended request was itself refused. The original diagnostic did not identify the occupying request.
resolution.correction: The isolated synthetic Vite fixture binds the tagged HTTP read to the real snapshot frame and reply by writer request ID. The test gates browser reads, observes server-side idle before post-undo contention and checks cancellation, drain and restored output. Product admission and persistence are unchanged.
resolution.prevention: The negative control verifies the busy probe and refused intended request, then verifies cancellation leaves the writer occupied until its matching reply drains. The positive control checks the same holder completes at revision 2 while the first browser read receives BUSY. Ubuntu and Windows verify browser recovery and the exact removal and undo receipts in SQLite.

items.source: Original Windows run 45046352101, archives/runs/20261122T165618.491721Z-d3e98934/test-report.json. Recurrence in run 45387261521, archives/runs/windows-change-45387261521-1/test-report.json. Earlier related finding: windows-desktop-fixture-acl-preparation-timeout. Third occurrence: PR 84 run 45468479291, archives/observations/pr-84-45468479291/index.json (SHA-256 399e91e184e8742b868013470e7b32f53890b4bc651d4d14dec5752058392f65). Windows workspace-timeframe log SHA-256 ffe18daefd5643711fa8cc8c29da1765ca07845151d9e2cec85f157936895521. Fourth occurrence: PR 84 run 45489014243, archives/runs/windows-change-45489014243-1/test-report.json. Windows workspace-timeframe log SHA-256 3983a2e110c148f7de8f3123bf32a07742115f22b613300633cdf96b3cf9556d. Fifth occurrence: authenticated Windows pull request run 45543157570, attempt 1, https://github.com/kacoyi/scopehub/actions/runs/45543157570. The report and all bound logs were verified by the diagnostic resolver. The workspace-timeframe log SHA-256 is 116aa1c7ccb5b25ed312da8caf40f272614331063745bc9b075172d4164eee54.
items.observation: The first occurrence reported two explicit fixture preparations and one application provisioning timeout while Rust and Python overlapped. M0-071 removed redundant fixture calls and verified native refusal, cleanup and recovery. In the second occurrence, cargo test --locked --workspace ran with Python on a separate runner. Four native desktop library tests failed at prepare/powershell-timeout before their expected assertions, with 24 of 28 passing. One failure was explicit fixture preparation and the others reached application provisioning outside its slot. Prior instrumented Windows logs show up to four overlapping ACL helpers, but the recurrence lacks timing inside the PowerShell process. The core Rust log SHA-256 is ded2d67bbfd496c03ff04f9e0b715eb8f76d44523dc49a81fe6c20cf42a35dfa. Independent Astra review of 0739be2 found that the release regression uses an arbitrary mutex and cannot catch the two actual paths losing their shared slot. Third occurrence: four originally independent workspace-timeframe fixtures (:144, :215, :556 and :652) stopped in workspace_bridge --prepare-profile-root with (prepare, powershell-timeout), before Vite or SQLite. The fourth failed with no other workspace case running. The browser launches separate bridge processes outside the prior Tauri test-only mutex. The same four Linux cases and the three Windows indicator delivery and recovery controls passed. The failed Windows process contains no measured internal stage beyond the PowerShell timeout. Fourth occurrence: the same reviewed native Windows inputs used one 64-profile setup before both workers. The ordinary PR producer returned prepare/powershell-timeout after 10.290 seconds and started zero browser cases. The same-input task had prepared 64 roots in 735 ms. The native Rust controls passed on a different Windows host. Fifth occurrence: three ordinary workspace fixtures (workspace.spec.mjs:144, :215 and :556) stopped in workspace_bridge --prepare-profile-root at prepare/powershell-timeout. The other cases recorded 54 passes and one skip. No original log reports first script execution or exact slow ACL work.

resolution.cause: Ordinary workspace preparation depended on a PowerShell child reaching completion under the existing timeout. The archived failures do not identify the internal stage that stalled.
resolution.correction: Use the same supervised native Windows ACL policy for preparation and opening in the ordinary desktop and workspace bridge. Keep the existing deadlines and refusal controls.
resolution.prevention: The hosted workspace and desktop transport checks ran the ordinary browser paths, and Rust exercised native refusal and supervised cleanup. The resolved archive reports windows-change-45554913043-1 (source 1a71e272d3abd9fabb8ce49ed3316289f264786a, SHA-256 744a0d549a2beaae9de5976e09269ce28afe31ddb9d8625ca9c9bc45eceac7c7) and windows-change-45555389370-1 (source 150a733a91a160455582c1e485b2f8db25a66f83, SHA-256 0b0814940fac485a6e3655ce94cb15c264c4d8566328bdbd737699c5d45d5736) each retain two prepare/powershell-timeout failures before chart execution. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

items.source: Authenticated Windows PR 42 run 45042311132. Original report and logs are retained under archives/runs/20261122T161306.780775Z-67e5702f/test-report.json.
items.observation: The Python process reached its 900-second deadline after printing test 567 of 568. The report records a 900.015-second timeout. Earlier completed suites took 645.078 and 696.188 seconds. Other native checks also took longer in the failed run.

resolution.cause: The fixed 900-second deadline expired during complete discovery on a slower Windows runner. Eighteen other checks slowed by factors of about 1.23 to 1.69 compared with a passing main run. The final test name showed progress at expiry. Its individual Windows duration in the failed run is unknown.
resolution.correction: Set the Windows deadline for python-contracts-workers to 1200 seconds. The 645.078-second passing suite multiplied by the observed 1.693 slowdown gives about 1092 seconds. Serial and overlapped dispatch read the same bounded catalog setting. The Linux deadline remains 900 seconds.
resolution.prevention: Dispatch regression covers both Windows execution paths, the Linux fallback and sibling budgets. A one-second forced timeout preserved the original progress and timeout output. Full discovery completed on both platforms in PR run 45058420352.

items.source: Authenticated main Windows run 45101333252, archives/runs/20261123T024037.246404Z-9bf7f2cb/test-report.json.
items.observation: Desktop localization was the only failed check in run 45101333252. Its first Simplified Chinese sample-button assertion expired after 5000 ms at desktop.spec.mjs:20. The other 13 cases passed. The original log references a screenshot and error context absent from the published artifact. The warm Cargo build took 0.25 seconds and the check took 23.203 seconds. Nearby warm Windows runs 45070244999 and 45098363813 passed in 14.531 and 17.938 seconds. These are whole-check timings and leave the original entry and locale at expiry unknown. A controlled 6.2-second main-module delay reproduced the assertion locally while the startup page was already in Chinese. Under the same delay the repaired check reached the Chinese workspace in 6.9 seconds. A local pair with fresh browser contexts and the same Vite server mounted in 243 ms after forced optimization and 207 ms after the graph was warm. An English context mounted normally and exposed the English label, isolating a locale mismatch from startup readiness. The retained comparison is archives/observations/M1-033/local-startup-comparison/SHA256SUMS (SHA-256 a63778aa4067258f633985df2c54707c8a3b1243b67c072e28c164b72466310a).

resolution.cause: The test started a five-second language-specific control assertion at document load while the application entry was still importing asynchronously. The controlled delay confirmed that the assertion could expire on an already localized startup page. The original Windows diagnostic cannot establish the reason for that run's missing control.
resolution.correction: Observe a mounted desktop through the shared preview startup helper and its existing ten-second budget, then assert the document locale and real localized button. Use the same observer to report the terminal entry failure in the localized recovery case.
resolution.prevention: The bounded 6.2-second delay, localized preference and reload flows and shared fatal and stalled startup checks passed on Ubuntu and Windows in run 45105648304 at 01c5aab. The native Windows report is retained at archives/runs/20261123T032538.318226Z-f085ac2b/test-report.json (SHA-256 6fd06399e41c7dc5ba89b5fe97174d6308d8f488aa2424428ba16bc5b40b9813).

Catalog rows gained that stable identifier and product_progress copied it into the published object.

items.source: Independent M0-077 review of the source tree committed as e6adefd.
items.observation: A synthetic shared graph with nine distinct targets triggered 511 reads. A long acyclic source chain raised RecursionError. A short cycle was already rejected correctly. Project and architecture commands both expand the engineering index.

resolution.cause: The first recursive reader detected cycles along a path but read a shared document for each reference. Finite deep or shared graphs could exhaust the runtime stack or multiply work.

items.source: Owner observation of a 3h51m delivery and protected workflow 45118576843 / main workflow 45121572762 for PR 52.
items.observation: Three real-Git verification-scope regressions launched 430 Git processes on Ubuntu. The Windows Python suite is a major component of the protected feedback path. Existing iteration instructions also prescribe overlapping local checks.

resolution.cause: Fixture builders repeatedly read an unchanged commit and initialized Git configuration in four processes per repository. The selector verified checkout metadata and each pull request parent in separate Git calls, including for unusable events. Local feedback instructions also prescribed overlapping profiles.
resolution.correction: Read immutable identities together and reuse commits already observed by each isolated fixture. Group a product slice with its contract and regression, show the first usable interaction early and select feedback profiles for their added coverage.
resolution.prevention: The same synchronize, pull request and push scenarios ran three times per revision on Linux. Git invocations via PATH fell from 162 to 76, 136 to 75 and 132 to 61 respectively. Added real repositories cover tag substitution, an extra merge parent and a tracked HEAD path. The ordinary protected run now retains per-case Python timings. Weekly review pairs speed with failures, retries and post-merge defects.

items.source: Independent M0-078 review of 8bf926a..41c60a8 before protected CI.
items.observation: A Git directory inherited from the caller could redirect the new timing fixture outside its temporary repository. The first positive comparison also started from a synthetic report that failed the hosted publication schema.

resolution.correction: Isolate the Git environment for synthetic timing and publication repositories. Stage schema-valid reports, named logs and distinct real merge commits through the ordinary Actions artifact entry point before comparing the resulting PR and main samples.

items.source: RustSec advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0594 and the online dependency review on bea74a5.

The upstream issue concerns private cookies on fork-capable platforms and excludes Windows from its affected OS list. GitHub's open glib alert is covered by a separate existing disposition.

resolution.cause: Cargo.lock retained cookie 0.18.2 when RustSec published RUSTSEC-2026-0594. The shared online review detected it, but ran after expensive checks on a full selection.
resolution.correction: Resolve the published 0.18.3 patch under the existing Tauri and Wry constraints. Update the inventory and notices, and move the selected dependency review immediately after environment and project-state.

items.source: Repository-wide review and direct comparison of the release selector with readiness bindings at bea74a5.
items.observation: The 43-check release profile and its candidate verifier omit nine task-cadence obligations for workspace and decision records, indicators, local import, model connections and state migrations. A release run cannot supply this evidence to readiness.

resolution.cause: Both the harness and candidate verifier independently excluded every task-cadence check before considering release obligations.
resolution.correction: A shared selection combines the existing release baseline with checks bound by milestones, acceptance, scenarios and explicit release policy. The retained-candidate verifier requires every selected check and its original log.
resolution.prevention: The production catalog regression covers the nine omissions. Synthetic release runs add independent obligations at all four bindings and exercise platform and implementation limits. Hosted candidate tests verify a complete report and reject a missing selection, missing result or changed log.

items.source: 2026-11-23 repository audit of native CSV preview, publication and readback using a synthetic futures row.
items.observation: A source row declared timeframe 1m, timezone UTC and cumulative volume while the approved mapping declared 5m, Asia/Shanghai and per_bar. The preview normalized the row and the newly published revision returned 13:10 UTC and volume 150 with the wrong 5m semantics.

resolution.cause: The native bar normalizer compared source quantity unit, price adjustment and venue with the mapping, while source timeframe, timezone and volume semantics were treated as auxiliary data without checking their values.
resolution.correction: Compare each explicit declaration with the reviewed native bar mapping before producing a normalized row. Full-file publication and folder inspection use the same check, retain the locator and display source-specific diagnostics in both desktop languages.
resolution.prevention: Worker tests cover compatible and conflicting declarations, bounded preview, source locators and alternate valid series. The real desktop bridge verifies late conflicts cannot publish and the frozen readback survives. The folder browser excludes contradictory files from its change set. The M1-034 receipt records these regressions.

items.observation: Rows declaring a bar end, a different calendar or session, or an equity instrument still normalized and passed the complete-file check under a bar-start dated futures mapping. The declaration list did not cover the formal mapping and series fields.

Inspect every applicable unbound semantic declaration, preserving exact identifiers and source formatting, permitted equivalents, the original reserved economic headers and established custom bindings. Whole-file publication and folder review use the same comparison as row preview.
resolution.prevention: Independent examples and both language catalogs cover every semantic property in the canonical schema. Worker regressions cover conflicting and matching values, historical header aliases, active interpretation rules and data bindings. Real profile publication and folder review verify late conflicts and unchanged accepted data. The failed baseline and passing task receipt are retained.

items.source: contracts/reviews/2026-11-23-continuity-audit.json, finding untriaged-failure-handoff
items.observation: A narrower passing run dropped an earlier executed failure from startup and recovery, an unrelated manual run could cover the normal CI failure, and unchanged historical evidence could close a newly reported defect.

resolution.correction: Report unresolved local failures and incomplete scans, validate matching rechecks against the official report schema and logs, and inspect ordinary, manual and weekly verification separately. Register the repair checks at intake and require active plans to cover serious feedback.
resolution.prevention: The local check, harness preflight and protected history use the same feedback transition validation. The verified observation and occurrence bind to the archived passing checks. Regression tests cover omissions, concurrent and malformed runs, stale weekly results, unchanged old receipts, a repeated finding and rejection before launching checks.

items.source: Required Windows run 45324432453 on #67, and two independent controlled subprocess reproductions using the unmodified worker and the 18 existing inputs.
items.observation: The Windows ownership test failed with 19 frames after hello for 18 requests. The retained Windows runner log does not record the extra frame body. resolution.correction: Submit the original requests through a controlled stdin sequence and observe a real event before matching terminal cancellation. Assert the unchanged 18 responses and verify each asynchronous frame against the active subscription and frozen sequence.

The re-review added ProcessFailed to the shared required observations at d4cea0d. items.source: Required Ubuntu transport check for PR 73, archives/runs/20261124T075459.275900Z-a4026d20/test-report.json, desktop-workspace-transport.log and the retained browser screenshot.
items.observation: The first open of a seeded published CSV stayed in the dialog with 'Unable to open the frozen chart.' The source button never appeared at line 194, so the test did not reach its controlled source write, revision proof or late acknowledgement. The hosted artifacts do not contain the underlying read reply. Locally, holding a genuine Rust-backed status read made the foreground frozen chart invoke receive retryable BUSY and reproduced that exact alert before any write. A separate unknown revision returned SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE and displayed the dedicated rejection.

resolution.cause: Foreground chart reads treated transient writer contention as terminal. Holding a real status read reproduced the hosted message. The hosted image and log do not identify the original response code.
resolution.correction: Retry an explicitly retryable BUSY read within its original deadline using its original request ID. Keep unavailable revisions and uncertain writes on their existing paths.
resolution.prevention: The transport regression separately opens a missing revision and a valid contended revision before exercising the delayed write, revision proof and late reply.

items.source: Independent review of df22f2a and inspection of the LocalRevisionDialog and LocalImportEditor foreground read entries.
items.observation: Closing the published CSV dialog aborts its lifetime, but the authenticated frozen chart read did not receive the signal. The editor likewise omitted cancellation and excluded chart reads from the Cancel control. With that control exposed and the old request wiring, both views submitted a second read after close or cancel and delivery of a held retryable BUSY response.

resolution.cause: The two foreground entries did not carry their cancellation signal through contention backoff.
resolution.correction: Pass the dialog lifetime or editor read signal through the bounded read. Cancelling or closing prevents another read and ignores a late result.
resolution.prevention: Both foreground regressions hold a retryable reply through cancellation and verify a single read, zero source writes and no stale chart.

items.source: Independent review of df22f2a and inspection of the native transport fixture's response barrier.
items.observation: The test waited on a resolver that a thrown dispatch could not settle. Its cleanup asserted the held reply, which could replace an earlier failure. A local malformed status request returned INVALID_ARGUMENT and the fixture surfaced a generic early completion error instead.

resolution.cause: A thrown dispatch could leave the original waiter unresolved and a cleanup assertion could hide the first failure.
resolution.correction: Observe the real bounded dispatch, retain early error codes and make release independent of any assertion about the result.
resolution.prevention: The transport regression checks an INVALID_ARGUMENT reply and a thrown dispatch, then reopens and releases the gate to verify cleanup.

Restore returned the original author text but switched the chart to the 5-minute 09:40 UTC result at 3.2%. The focused Chromium regression reproduced the reset of the 15-minute control after the chart was removed.

resolution.correction: The workbench retains the accepted block timeframes with their validated definitions and original authored text. Preview changes stay with the draft.

items.source: Astra review of a5aba30 against 89867c9. The coordinator reproduced both cases on Ubuntu Tauri/WebKitGTK and retained observations/m2-029-edit-a5aba30/observations.json, SHA-256 d5b00e261d6fd832d9e2707de438e03013ce30d310d536312bac146dc5abd246.

items.source: Independent Standard Astra review of 6e3760446fb5e137e5aa610880c9c8763069f92e. The three failing editor interactions are retained at archives/observations/m2-030-state-view-cc4a363/review-red/results.json (SHA-256 92c91a5982387c83f23491c7ee5caec9f93ddb4454c19bf3de89b968a75466ec).

items.source: Owner feedback on 2026-11-24, six authenticated full Windows PR checks and the coordinator observing that independent implementation was waiting on hosted acceptance. The original reports are retained under archives/runs at the listed diagnostic identities.
items.observation: Routine validation repeatedly exceeded the existing 15-minute feedback objective. The Windows Python test check alone consumed 822.6 and 812.2 seconds. From a shared base, repeated intermediate runs and serial waits consumed time while independent product work could proceed. The earlier timing work had not prevented these further oversized cycles.

resolution.cause: Windows ran independent groups in series, and repeated Git observations inflated the Python check. The prior weekly timing review recorded overruns without requiring the coordinator to carry a measured recovery into the next handoff.
resolution.correction: Run Windows core, browser and Python checks concurrently and collect their original outcomes in the protected job. On ordinary warm full PR 45399239580, the required workflow took 866 seconds and used 2805 runner seconds. The four original PR controls had medians of 1851 and 2598 seconds respectively. Record the separately measured main push in M0-091.
resolution.prevention: Normal status and CI associate recurring comparable overruns with corrective work. Require actual recovery for the same event, coverage, cache and repaired code. Product teams can demonstrate and review an independent slice while hosted verification proceeds. Retain the fixed controls, named outcomes and successful and failed attempts in the delivery review.

items.source: Authenticated ordinary main pushes 45371103989, 45376798249, 45383842961, 45389486376 and 45394539742. The original Windows reports and their logs are retained under archives/runs at the listed diagnostic identities.
items.observation: Five successful full main pushes using the previous Windows scheduler and a warm Cargo cache took 1720, 1940, 1970, 1588 and 1932 seconds. The objective is 900 seconds. A successful ordinary full main push containing the repair must establish its own elapsed time, coverage, cache state and runner occupancy.

resolution.cause: The previous Windows scheduler serialized independent checks. After the first repair, later protected main observations still exceeded the budget or failed. The retained original attempts show their own elapsed times and verdicts.
resolution.correction: The repaired main ran the original groups through separate Windows producers with a protected aggregate. The exact comparable push 45478822360 succeeded in 897 seconds with 3236 runner seconds. See archives/observations/m0-091-closure-c4f07b3/review.json (SHA-256 2246234ef554b05453ea89e011d6bc76e18b9a7caea48d43bf9322011ce7ba49).
resolution.prevention: The coordinator follows repeat overruns in ordinary status and CI and assigns corrective work. The active development AI resolves the first failed original and verifies the affected regression. Before closure, confirm that the latest specific protected main is successful, full, warm, comparable and within budget, with a matching exact Windows receipt.

items.source: Independent Astra review of 02a5176, retained in archives/observations/m0-087-verification-review/astra-02a5176.txt, finding 1.
items.observation: Git status configuration hid real untracked files from the source identity used by project:ci. The same cleanliness claim had no guard for hidden index flags or caller-configured submodule ignore settings.

resolution.correction: Inspect the staged index and untracked paths together, disable status visibility shortcuts, and inspect populated submodules for hidden changes before accepting a clean checkout.

items.source: Independent Astra reviews of 02a5176, 1e03799 and fc0fa8f retained in archives/observations/m0-087-verification-review/astra-02a5176.txt, archives/observations/m0-087-verification-review/astra-1e03799.txt and archives/observations/m0-087-verification-review/astra-fc0fa8f.txt. The retained Windows reports were replayed against the earlier control and candidate in archives/observations/m0-087-verification-review/timing-review-replay.json. The new regressions reproduced the three fc0fa8f findings in archives/observations/m0-087-verification-review/shared-eligibility-red.log.
items.observation: Deep JSON erased the normal CI result regardless of its verdict, and a malformed sample suppressed valid timing observations. An incomplete intake placeholder or unreadable cache file could permanently prevent the corresponding run from being observed again. Follow-up review found that a missing check exit code still suppressed unrelated overruns and that incomplete or conflicting clocks and stale retry warnings could misstate the current observation. The fc0fa8f review reproduced a report with no harness run ID suppressing a Windows artifact retry and a retained split clock qualifying after removal of a required producer.

resolution.cause: Partial and malformed observations could affect the whole timing view, and capture and review used different completeness tests.
resolution.correction: Isolate corrupt records, require one eligibility rule with harness identity and recorded time, and reject conflicting or incomplete attempt clocks. A persisted Windows split clock requires exactly one core, browser and Python producer.
resolution.prevention: Exercise passed, failed and blocked CI results with mixed and deep telemetry, malformed check rows, incompatible clocks, omitted producers and bounded retry of only missing platform evidence.

items.source: Independent Astra reviews of 02a5176, 1e03799 and fc0fa8f retained in archives/observations/m0-087-verification-review/astra-02a5176.txt, archives/observations/m0-087-verification-review/astra-1e03799.txt and archives/observations/m0-087-verification-review/astra-fc0fa8f.txt.
items.observation: Budget escalation combined overruns across different cache or coverage cohorts and could lose repeated warm overruns after unrelated cold runs. Two ordinary PRs observed in separate worktrees did not form one local review window. Reusing an existing corrective task hid the action to associate newly observed reports with its finding. Follow-up review found that complete pre-existing local observations and compatible partial local and shared observations were not consolidated into the shared window. The fc0fa8f review reproduced incompatible complete samples selecting the first arrival and losing the conflict at the next worktree handoff.

resolution.cause: The escalation used mixed timing cohorts and worktree-local observations, and an incompatible sample could become the shared winner based on arrival order.
resolution.correction: Use repository-shared compact observations and compare equivalent platform, cache and check outcomes. Preserve incompatible sample pairs as ambiguous and expose unassociated evidence for the active corrective task.
resolution.prevention: Exercise fresh worktrees, compatible local and shared captures, both conflict arrival orders, prior ownership, warm and cold cohorts, and a complete reuse that makes no remote timing requests.

items.source: Independent Astra review of b7b2622, retained at archives/observations/m0-087-integration-main-handoff/astra-b7b2622.txt (SHA-256 7626ec51000d5c00274d69d2a432490ca22d603984093b0486598f294dfaec63).
items.observation: With the measurement task still planned, a repair PR can remove its ownership from the named main-push finding and mark the finding addressed using the repair task's regression receipt. Project loading, history comparison and integration assessment then pass without querying timing. The regression receipt covers the repair and cannot establish a main-push result before the repair reaches main.

resolution.cause: Removing the planned measurement task from the finding allowed an existing repair receipt to satisfy ordinary feedback closure. Integration then skipped the addressed finding and did not require a protected main-push timing observation.
resolution.correction: Require the designated follow-up to stay linked and complete with a receipt for the same successful comparable Windows main push identified by the timing engine. Verify that the push contains the repair and is on protected base history. A later evidence-only closure can use the records profile.
resolution.prevention: Replay the premature addressed transition through project loading, history comparison and integration assessment. Exercise successful records closure and reject missing, failed, over-budget, stale, or mismatched main-push evidence, including a newer over-budget observation after an earlier success.

items.source: Independent Astra review of 59f4c0d, retained at archives/observations/m0-087-integration-main-handoff/astra-59f4c0d.txt (SHA-256 82cce7e326a1f2b61fc880fbddf77cdf9ec38c4a80f0a873b9d62c2b89aaf083).
items.observation: The candidate policy supplies the only lookup key for the main-push closure check. A candidate can misspell the key, remove the follow-up owner from the original finding and mark it addressed. The normal integration entry then reports technical readiness without a main-push observation, even when the protected base names the original finding.

resolution.cause: The candidate policy supplied the only lookup key for the main-push closure check. A typo or substitution hid the original finding and allowed premature closure to bypass timing validation.
resolution.correction: Read the established policy from the protected base and require the canonical M0-087 and M0-091 identities on first introduction. Block changes to the protected rule and require both governed findings and their task records to resolve.
resolution.prevention: Exercise typos, substitutions, policy removal, and missing records at the normal integration entry for a new rule and an established rule. Retain regressions for legitimate records closure and unrelated product PRs.

items.source: Independent review of cfdcff2 using a real Windows report's commands and result fields.
items.observation: A records fixture with a passed summary and its selected dependency-review omitted as blocked/not_selected passed the lane validator. With a successful producer job, the protected aggregate could return zero for that report.

resolution.cause: The scoped Windows validator accepted a passing report whose selected dependency check had been marked not selected.
resolution.correction: Require every selected scoped check to succeed and preserve the protected aggregate failure when a producer fails or is cancelled.
resolution.prevention: Run the scoped aggregate with authentic command and status fields, reject a selected omission and verify the aggregate failure guard through the retained failed pilot.

items.source: Independent review of cfdcff2 using a real two-parent merge and a stale pull request preview SHA.
items.observation: The selector requested full coverage when it could not trust the comparison. The protected aggregate repeated that comparison prerequisite and rejected the complete lane results even though the actual checkout and event parents agreed.

resolution.cause: The full Windows aggregate repeated the narrow comparison prerequisite after the selector had fallen back to full coverage.
resolution.correction: Verify the actual checkout and event parent identities independently of scope classification and accept full coverage when the comparison is uncertain.
resolution.prevention: Exercise a valid two-parent full fallback and reject the corresponding unverified or reduced-scope case while retaining the original lane evidence checks.

items.source: Authenticated PR 77 Windows Python producer on run 45384002726, retained at archives/runs/windows-change-45384002726-1/test-report.json with its original check log.
items.observation: The Python check failed after 528.907 seconds. Two of 665 cases errored when reading verification-scope.json from nested public staging. The enclosing producer exports SCOPEHUB_WINDOWS_LANE=python, which can select private lane staging inside those ordinary public staging calls and suppress the typed scope file.

resolution.cause: The Python producer's inherited SCOPEHUB_WINDOWS_LANE selected private staging inside ordinary nested staging calls.
resolution.correction: Select private producer staging with the explicit stage-windows-lane command. Public full, records and aggregate staging continue to emit their typed scope evidence.
resolution.prevention: Reproduce the original two named errors under the inherited producer environment, preserve their scope and report assertions, and verify explicit lane staging retains the failed lane report, logs and compact timing.

items.source: Independent Astra review of 3acb4aa. Replayed the authenticated run 45393623602 Python producer report and compact timing from archives/observations/m0-087-hosted-45393623602/producer-python/.
items.observation: The Windows aggregate accepted a warm compact sample with a boolean exit code in place of zero or a numeric coverage flag in place of a boolean. Removing task_id was also accepted as an explicit null. A mistyped or incomplete producer sample could therefore admit an otherwise warm run to the warm-cache timing comparison, even though the underlying check result remained valid.

resolution.cause: The aggregate compared compact timing with ordinary Python equality and read projected fields through get. It treated boolean and numeric values as equal and a missing task_id as an explicit null.
resolution.correction: Require every projected field and exact JSON type and value agreement with the report-derived projection. If optional compact timing is unreadable, incomplete, or incompatible, classify the lane cache as unknown and preserve the actual check rows, logs, and protected verification verdict.
resolution.prevention: Replay the authentic Windows Python producer and a complete warm-shaped copy, then reject a boolean exit code, a numeric coverage flag, and an omitted task_id. Exercise the protected aggregate with only the Python compact timing altered and verify that the original passing row is retained. Retain the independent Astra finding and approval.

items.source: Independent Astra review of 15093feb63dc8fa61c3401b69be1faadb4d3ef0f and focused confirmation on d1d04a3, retained under archives/observations/m4-016-d1d04a3/. Local browser reproduction at archives/runs/20261124T111053.555558Z-28236d9b/test-report.json.
items.observation: After a peer clears a shared bar selection, clicking the chart citation reads the new selection revision with a null target and rejects the jump. The composer still shows the old selected interval and enables Send for a draft until the core rejects the stale send. The real browser reproduced the enabled control with the draft, prior answer, and model request count unchanged.

resolution.cause: Citation navigation checked the new workspace snapshot while the composer continued to use the opening selection.
resolution.correction: Use the existing citation snapshot to invalidate only a composer binding superseded by same-workspace selection authority. Keep the draft and retain newer valid selections.
resolution.prevention: A real peer clears the selection. The browser verifies the draft and answer, fences the submit handler, observes no model traffic, and makes the same draft sendable after selecting a newer valid bar. A separate case preserves an already-valid newer binding when an older citation is rejected.

items.source: Independent Astra review of 15093feb63dc8fa61c3401b69be1faadb4d3ef0f and focused confirmation on d1d04a3, retained under archives/observations/m4-016-d1d04a3/. Local browser reproduction at archives/runs/20261124T111053.555558Z-28236d9b/test-report.json.
items.observation: After revealing a citation and returning to its focused row, a peer clears the shared selection. Enter on the same row rejects the jump, sends focus to the question field and scrolls the conversation to the bottom. The browser reproduction lost focus and moved the transcript scroll offset from 20 to 689 pixels after only a local snapshot read.

resolution.cause: The return flag drove both reopening focus and ordinary transcript scrolling. Rejection changed the flag while the same citation remained open.
resolution.correction: Keep focus and scroll in the evidence reading state after a rejection. A deliberate submit clears that state so ordinary follow-up behavior resumes.
resolution.prevention: The browser retries an earlier citation with Enter after a real peer clears the selection. It checks the focused row, exact transcript offset and local-only request. A separate deliberate follow-up verifies normal composer focus.

items.source: Authenticated PR 77 Windows browser producer on run 45387261521, retained through the canonical aggregate at archives/runs/windows-change-45387261521-1/test-report.json. The workspace-timeframe log (SHA-256 5968a19a764577fa36c336c9f6bea80f53830d9791a6679f5a82d2a5a2afc62d) and the reopened sample case attachments record the failed assertion and both browser fetch outcomes.
items.observation: The browser reported a single rejected selected-history fetch without headers. The same trace recorded two server receipts and admissions followed by two close events with status 200, with the second receipt arriving before the first close. The test expected consecutive receipt, admission and close triples, so it rejected the trace even after both closes arrived. The explicit retry while disconnected reported its own distinct rejected fetch.

resolution.cause: Chromium could admit a second physical HTTP request before the first socket close was logged. The test treated adjacent receipt, admission and close events as one request.
resolution.correction: Correlate each logical history fetch and physical HTTP attempt separately, drain trace output before judging the terminals and check each disconnected attempt against its own received, admitted and closed events.
resolution.prevention: Replay the authenticated interleaving, reject missing and repeated closes, and run the original reopened-sample UI case through response loss, a distinct explicit retry, history recovery, a genuine 403 and the original private undo.

items.source: Independent Astra review of 2b4835f, retained at archives/observations/m0-087-browser-request-attempts/astra-2b4835f.txt (SHA-256 5af56f834295b89aa7de1c6af3e6f5b558b459f8286bb4e7cb2ffd6480cdf226).
items.observation: The ordinary browser fixture withheld a real close until the same logical fetch was admitted again. The review reproduced the false timeout when Chromium makes one complete HTTP attempt. The generic observation also accepted two finished events for the same physical request on successful HTTP 200 and complete HTTP 403 paths because it only checked the first and last stages.

resolution.cause: The fixture delayed a real close until optional Chromium replay, and the generic observer accepted duplicate terminals when the last event still looked complete.
resolution.correction: Allow the real single-attempt or replayed socket sequence in the browser. Exercise the deterministic interleaving separately and require exactly one terminal per physical attempt after trace drain.
resolution.prevention: Keep the single-attempt red and green, reject a missing close and duplicate terminals for real HTTP 200 and 403 paths, and retain the established UI recovery and private undo assertions.

items.source: Original 46-of-48 local run at archives/observations/m0-087-browser-pilot-investigation/full/workspace-timeframe/results.json (SHA-256 92e10d2ac059435c03afee7266f2efe4e7ffa89a79252d9a3ecc5ba637ad4cab) and archives/observations/m0-087-browser-pilot-investigation/full/playwright.log (SHA-256 76aa6bfa79f1d431c47414dc211dd0d8f4ae7db73586f2a6984681d4bd431458). See the derived timeline at archives/observations/m0-087-browser-request-attempts/full-attribution.json.
items.observation: The two failed workers recorded the same end time, 12:08:41.514 UTC. The reopened sample browser observer reached its 18-second deadline after the 5.509-second delayed disconnect and a second host admission, while the fetch was still pending. The fixture budget can expire before the second request's 15-second watchdog. The concurrent parent-IPC case stopped at the Vite readiness gate with an empty child log and never exercised the IPC disconnect. The retained observations establish both failure boundaries and leave the underlying causes unresolved.

resolution.cause: The reopened history fixture gave its logical browser observer 18 seconds, even though the deliberate first-response hold was 5.5 seconds and an optional physical retry had its own 15-second preview watchdog. The retained run observed a 5.509-second hold, a second admission, the first close and a browser fetch still pending at the observer timeout. A controlled replay proved the observer could expire before a valid retry terminal. The concurrent Vite failure occurred before the parent-disconnect test body. The generic readiness error grouped child exit with deadline expiry and retained an empty output tail without the child, probe or cleanup chronology needed to distinguish them. Why the original second request remained pending, why the original Vite check failed and whether a shared host condition contributed remain unknown.
resolution.correction: Add the configured 5.5-second hold to the observer budget for the first faulted reopen only, yielding a finite 23.5-second wait. Keep the 15-second preview watchdog, ordinary 18-second observation, explicit retry and terminal assertions intact. Classify fixture readiness by owned listening evidence, fresh HTTP probes and monotonic child and cleanup events. Wait for stdio closure and serialize only allowlisted notices. The ordinary readiness deadline remains 10 seconds.
resolution.prevention: At the consumed browser observer, require a logical requestfailed terminal at controlled time 20.499 seconds and reject a headers-only request at 23.5 seconds. Keep the real recovered-history and private-undo assertions. At the readiness gate, distinguish strict EADDRINUSE after lease release from a live child held before listening. Check that neither starts a writer or creates a handoff, verify reaping, and retain the normal startup, IPC and POSIX signal cases. Record the bounded chronology below for any recurrence.

items.source: PR #77 Linux pilot run 45393623602. Original diagnostic archives/runs/20261124T122836.056903Z-08468273/test-report.json. Local red and green originals and the independent review are retained in archives/observations/m1-038-visible-csv/manifest.json (SHA-256 4928ae6909e34b510523343096c5b0182fa77626c9c29a4f633463266e5733bb).
items.observation: After a successful synthetic folder picker reply from the ordinary Data sources panel, the source workflow timed out at tests/ui/local-import.spec.mjs:419. The first page-wide exact Local CSV match resolved to a hidden h3 on 14 polls. The chart keeps its panel mounted while CSV review is active, and the import header uses the same text. The retrieved and archived artifacts contain the verification log but lack the local-import screenshot and trace listed in it. Two local repetitions on df99e89 first verified the visible import region and the retained hidden heading, then failed at the original locator. The failure screenshot shows equities/daily.csv in the visible editor. The browser report, screenshots and traces remain under .reports/m1-038-red/ (browser-results.json SHA-256 20e5b3ad323f0041973de5460fcf91ac90836027410eb72e7fa07e6c807cd536).

resolution.cause: A page-wide exact text locator selected the first Local CSV label in document order, which was inside the retained hidden chart panel after the visible CSV editor had opened.
resolution.correction: Verify the destination by the visible Local CSV import region. Scope its preview and file assertions to that editor and the invoking picker to the appropriate surface.
resolution.prevention: The ordinary-entry regression verifies independently specified equity and futures values, both cancellation paths, the resumed review and rejected settlement mapping. Two red traces and screenshots, two passing focused repetitions and the matching task report are retained by digest. Astra Standard independently reviewed the red and green observations and approved f230621.

items.source: Independent Astra review of d28f749, observation m0-087-workspace-readiness-d28f749, transcript SHA-256 3a8c4938345409ca0dd3aa9883fda79498009e4ae77cab3bbeba3176e86ac427.
items.observation: A successful HTTP response from a previous listener was accepted when the request started before the new child signaled listening and completed after that signal. The original local readiness stall supplies no observation of this sequence.

resolution.cause: The readiness loop tested for the child's listening flag after awaiting the HTTP response. A probe sent to an older listener could return HTTP 200 after the target child reported listening and be accepted as the new child's health result.
resolution.correction: Open a fresh unpooled HTTP connection for each probe and snapshot owned listening evidence before sending it. Only a successful probe initiated after the target child's IPC listening event or its POSIX CLI stdout notice can establish readiness.
resolution.prevention: Hold the old server's response, stop its listener, start the replacement and signal listening, then deliver the old HTTP 200. Require the gate to disregard that response and observe a separate socket at the replacement. Keep the real claimed-port and normal startup regressions.

items.source: Independent Astra review of d28f749, observation m0-087-workspace-readiness-d28f749, transcript SHA-256 3a8c4938345409ca0dd3aa9883fda79498009e4ae77cab3bbeba3176e86ac427.
items.observation: Truncating the child output before redaction left 14 characters of a synthetic fixture capability in the serialized startup error. The original local readiness stall retained an empty child log.

resolution.cause: The recorder truncated the raw child output before applying redaction. A synthetic handoff token split across chunks could straddle the tail boundary, leaving a 14-character suffix without the prefix or full-token pattern that redaction recognized.
resolution.correction: Keep the existing bounded capture private and serialize only fixed, allowlisted diagnostic notices after child stdio closes. Neither the failure string nor the attached diagnostic includes the raw tail.
resolution.prevention: Drive a split synthetic token through the truncation boundary and verify that its suffix is absent from both the error string and serialized startup object. Check that the allowlisted cleanup notice survives normal stdio drainage and keep the separately retained forced-kill evidence.

items.source: Independent Astra review of d28f749, observation m0-087-workspace-readiness-d28f749, transcript SHA-256 3a8c4938345409ca0dd3aa9883fda79498009e4ae77cab3bbeba3176e86ac427.
items.observation: The intentionally held fixture spends its two-second failure budget on Vite import and configuration before the controlled hold exists. A slow but valid configuration can fail the test before it observes the binding phase. This timing finding applies to the regression fixture introduced after the original local stalls.

resolution.cause: The short timeout in the intentionally held fixture began during Vite import and configuration. Valid but slow configuration could exhaust it before the fixture reported that it had reached the hold.
resolution.correction: Keep the ordinary monotonic 10-second startup deadline. Anchor the test-only 500 ms hold timeout to the observed held-before-listen event, which must arrive within the startup window. Keep the existing bounded cleanup.
resolution.prevention: Delay setup by 700 ms to exceed the short hold budget, then require the actual hold event and the full 500 ms before the live-child timeout. Verify normal exit and drained output with no writer, handoff or forced kill. The reviewed local sample observed the hold at 827 ms, deadline at 1327 ms and stdio close at 1334 ms.

items.source: Independent Astra re-review of b372142, transcript archives/observations/m0-087-workspace-readiness-d28f749/astra-b372142.txt (SHA-256 969fa72837fde8c64aa3800d4e8b07ec76ea6fec1617ac22ddfc08c4b4b12b90).
items.observation: The POSIX Vite CLI listener observer reads a combined stdout and stderr tail during stdout callbacks. A Local notice on stderr followed by unrelated stdout produces a false listening event. Stderr between two chunks of a valid stdout notice prevents that event. The real signal-path run passed and the original local stalls remain unattributed.

resolution.cause: The POSIX CLI listening parser ran on stdout callbacks but inspected a tail that already mixed stdout and stderr. Unrelated stdout could expose a Local notice written only to stderr. A stderr write between two stdout chunks could also split a valid notice in the parser's input.
resolution.correction: Feed only the owned child's stdout into an independent line parser. Keep at most 256 characters of an unfinished line, discard an oversized line through its newline, strip ANSI sequences and accept only the complete Vite loopback notice for the requested port. Keep failure output allowlisted.
resolution.prevention: Use the actual stream handler to reject a stderr-only notice followed by unrelated stdout and to accept a split stdout notice separated by a stderr warning. Retain the reviewed 13-case local run covering POSIX SIGINT and SIGTERM, parent IPC and ordinary development and ubuntu-preview startup.

items.source: Third PR 77 Linux pilot, archives/runs/20261124T122836.056903Z-08468273/test-report.json, transport log, screenshot and native-frozen-chart-admission attachment. The local failed report and raw trace are retained at archives/observations/m0-090-native-snapshot/local-red/results.json and archives/observations/m0-090-native-snapshot/local-red/native-snapshot-admission.json. Focused passing evidence and both reviews are indexed by archives/observations/m0-090-native-snapshot/SHA256SUMS (SHA-256 4cd1efab3320f4d5ddee6a0e9b4025babb366ec261c1255c4ada4a56cff55e93).
items.observation: The desktop transport test correctly displayed the unavailable revision and recorded one SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE read with no source writes. The independent snapshot at line 218 returned ok:false before the published read gate or delayed native write. The hosted artifact omits the failed snapshot's code. In a local 22-run comparison, one run reproduced the same assertion and recorded two successful native snapshots, then the unused companion preview's startup snapshot, then the independent proof refused with BUSY. Passing runs also showed the inverse ordering, with the companion refused at HTTP 429 when the independent proof won admission.

resolution.cause: In the local reproduction, the unused companion preview issued a startup snapshot after both native snapshots completed. Its admitted request contended with the independent proof on the shared writer lane. The hosted failure did not record the code or occupying request.
resolution.correction: Use the authorized Rust-backed transport without mounting a second browser for native-only cases. Keep browser preview mounting available to browser workflows.
resolution.prevention: The native regression verifies explicit chart rejection without a write, BUSY while a real Rust reply is held, the original selection after drain, and revision 2 after the delayed acknowledgement. Twenty repetitions of each focused case and nine browser source compatibility cases passed. The correction and cleanup passed independent review and matching task verification.

items.source: Independent Standard Astra review of d688cf0 retained in archives/observations/m0-090-native-snapshot/review/initial.txt (SHA-256 cfa203598bca649b271e53db862522265ffa21e8a9828797110f19e5a7a04c29). Narrow rereview of 9732834 is retained at archives/observations/m0-090-native-snapshot/review/cleanup.txt (SHA-256 4a2c304878ba5ff74c940befb448c19eb48896faa76edb4bfc7875dc783f82bf).
items.observation: The native source test attempts its first attachment before releasing three pending test barriers. With an injected scenario error followed by an attachment error, the fixture entered attachment with all barriers still pending and Playwright reported the attachment error as primary.

resolution.cause: The first awaited attachment preceded all release calls, and a failure in finally could replace the scenario error.
resolution.correction: Release the three barriers before attaching diagnostics. Preserve a prior scenario error and log a secondary attachment failure. Propagate a sole attachment failure.
resolution.prevention: The controlled before, after and attachment-only reports under archives/observations/m0-090-native-snapshot/cleanup-probe verify barrier release and the original error. The corrected native transport suite and narrow independent rereview passed.

items.source: Coordinator's ordinary handoff probe in the verification-cost checkout at df99e89, archives/observations/m0-087-budget-recovery-proof-74e3ec3/unmeasured-disposition-probe.json, SHA-256 90338eddc483c7f1a2be4df0d695af8d5ba6d11c589ed1dd6d623a858630ea3d.
items.observation: Four genuine comparable warm Windows pull requests took 1702, 1736, 1966 and 2088 seconds. With no successful repaired elapsed observation, changing only the issue disposition to addressed made handoff report the timing finding as addressed with no next action. A successful corrective check or historical issue disposition does not establish that a comparable ordinary PR or main push recovered the budget.

resolution.cause: Budget handoff treated the historical issue disposition as evidence of recovered elapsed timing.
resolution.correction: Keep the issue disposition separate from the measured recovery. Require a successful ordinary observation with the repaired inputs, same scope and comparable coverage and cache. Keep main push and PR recovery independent.
resolution.prevention: Replay the genuine warm PR controls with the issue disposition changed in memory and require an actionable pending result. Exercise accepted and rejected recovery with modeled clocks.

items.source: Independent Standard Astra review of 74e3ec3724fb528195aba44bfb301eb053f40fbe in the verification-cost checkout, archives/observations/m0-087-budget-recovery-proof-74e3ec3/astra-74e3ec3.pending.txt lines 3–15, SHA-256 2ce1e3de9f98c08de421f3e510ac333112b39486f60100b1ff459eb5b78b1c5a.
items.observation: Ordinary handoff accepted run 16 as recovery after the retained timing for linked overrun 18 disappeared. It accepted a single-parent descendant as a PR preview and rejected a genuine two-parent preview containing the repair through its first parent. It could not measure recovery from a within-budget median increase. After a measured recovery it dropped the still-active owner for two new overruns and mixed old runs into a false new sustained-growth window.

resolution.cause: Recovery compared only locally present reports, accepted an arbitrary descendant as an Actions PR checkout, and routed recurrences using mixed pre-recovery and post-recovery timing windows.
resolution.correction: Require evidence to follow every linked observation. Verify the actual merge parents in local Git or in the retained checkout observation, and accept correction ancestry on either tested parent. Choose the diagnosed timing window and restart comparison windows after recovery while keeping an active task owner.
resolution.prevention: Cover a missing later control, single-parent and misordered PR checkouts, legitimate first-parent repair, retained proof without a local preview object, sustained growth, and independently attributable recurrence.

items.source: Independent Astra review of actual ordinary PR 45393623602. The original compact samples and Actions jobs are retained in archives/observations/m0-087-hosted-45393623602/timing.json in the verification-cost checkout, SHA-256 593318f3ee6eedffc331ebd2ac3b2be57c46778714170d9c6b6ff7453936bd59.
items.observation: The Ubuntu harness failed and the Windows verification path completed in 933 seconds. The overall Actions workflow failed. The exact attempt contains both compact samples and a completed bound matrix clock. Handoff reported missing artifacts and incomplete clocks and attempted to retrieve the available data again.

resolution.cause: The collector used success eligibility to decide whether failed diagnostic artifacts and completed job clocks were present.
resolution.correction: Treat definite capture completeness independently of workflow success. Reuse the complete mixed-platform failed capture and suppress its obsolete missing-data notices.
resolution.prevention: Replay both authentic artifacts and the matrix clock for Actions run 45393623602 twice. Require the original failure, the original elapsed values and zero repeat retrievals.

items.source: Inspection of the ordinary integration scope and feedback history gates at df99e89, with the open Windows main-push budget finding and the protected push workflow.
items.observation: The integration scope rejects an open major finding linked to a changed delivery task. Keeping the repair task unfinished blocks integration, and transferring the main-push finding to a newly planned owner still blocks integration. A post-repair ordinary main push cannot occur until the reviewed repair enters main. A completed, evidenced repair needs a bounded handoff without resolving the original timing finding.

resolution.cause: The integration gate blocked the open major main-push finding while it belonged to the repair. Transferring it to a newly planned task still left it in the changed delivery scope. The required main-push observation could only occur after the repair merged.
resolution.correction: Permit the named main-push finding to stay open with M0-091 as the independent measurement task. Require the exact protected PR jobs and successful comparable PR timing, an archived regression receipt, and a repair introduced by the candidate before allowing the pending handoff.
resolution.prevention: Exercise the ordinary integration entry with real Git ancestry and verify that the resulting main push selects full verification. Reject unresolved PR timing, missing or failed jobs, stale or unbound receipts, records-only changes, and a follow-up that cannot start.

items.source: Independent Standard Astra read-only re-review of 6c11bbbe6134ad78105e5c1100df994e3ce3ec76 in the verification-cost checkout, archives/observations/m0-087-budget-recovery-proof-74e3ec3/review/astra-6c11bbb-hold.txt, finding 1, SHA-256 b980be4c345dac49d76a5bba1a379430721ac9cec92b2280f4e4d0852c08bc42.
items.observation: Ordinary CI reported a completed failed pull request while a cached success clock for the same attempt still proved budget recovery after the authenticated job lookup failed. The authenticated workflow failure must also survive an ordinary offline reread of the cache.

resolution.cause: Timing could still merge a stale successful job clock when the authenticated workflow verdict for the same attempt was failed and its job endpoint was unavailable.
resolution.correction: Treat the authenticated failure as a separately retained observation for the exact attempt. The common live and offline clock predicate discards incompatible conclusions while retaining diagnostics for matching failed clocks.
resolution.prevention: Pass a stale matching success through the regular CI entry with job retrieval and capture unavailable, then reread the normally retained failure offline. Require pending recovery and no stale elapsed proof.

items.source: Independent Standard Astra read-only re-review of 6c11bbbe6134ad78105e5c1100df994e3ce3ec76 in the verification-cost checkout, archives/observations/m0-087-budget-recovery-proof-74e3ec3/review/astra-6c11bbb-hold.txt, finding 2, SHA-256 b980be4c345dac49d76a5bba1a379430721ac9cec92b2280f4e4d0852c08bc42.
items.observation: A median increase from 600/600/600 to 730/730/930 seconds was routed as sustained growth, but one 730-second repaired run cleared it as a budget overrun. In the reverse case, an isolated 930-second observation in the original 600/600/930 baseline prevented recovery after three repaired 600-second observations.

resolution.cause: Recovery categorized the finding from any linked overrun and excluded original trend windows containing any individual overrun.
resolution.correction: Use the original ordinary three-run budget and consecutive median-window predicates on the linked observation history. A single slow observation does not change a diagnosed median regression into recurring budget overruns.
resolution.prevention: Test the 930-second observation separately in the original and degraded windows, require three comparable repaired runs for the median case, and require one successful within-budget run after a genuine repeated budget breach. Keep incomplete comparison history pending.

items.source: Independent Standard Astra read-only re-review of cf81feb317a3ccaf02d6dbf8421d94821231c7e3 in the verification-cost checkout, archives/observations/m0-087-budget-recovery-proof-74e3ec3/review/astra-cf81feb-hold.txt, finding 1, SHA-256 da547ac74a4ceead29ff1722078ea8cece10b40641fc4cffb0edfed2f005815f.
items.observation: Regular CI correctly returned failed and pending when a known failed attempt could not enter its timing capture. An immediate ordinary offline reread then recovered the same run from an old success clock because the current authenticated failure had not been retained independently of the capture lock or capture error.

resolution.cause: Authenticated failure reached the live view in memory, while saving it depended on the job capture writer and its lock.
resolution.correction: Atomically retain a separate record for the exact authenticated failed attempt and conclusion before job capture, and consult it in the common live and offline clock predicate.
resolution.prevention: Read ordinary offline timing immediately after both a real held capture lock and a capture error. Preserve the failed conclusion and leave budget recovery pending without a second successful capture.

items.source: Independent Standard Astra read-only re-review of cf81feb317a3ccaf02d6dbf8421d94821231c7e3 in the verification-cost checkout, archives/observations/m0-087-budget-recovery-proof-74e3ec3/review/astra-cf81feb-hold.txt, finding 2, SHA-256 da547ac74a4ceead29ff1722078ea8cece10b40641fc4cffb0edfed2f005815f.
items.observation: The diagnosed baseline was 600/600/930 seconds, followed by 730/730/730. Repaired runs at 700/700/700 remained pending with the full evidence. Removing one original 600-second sample allowed an older 630-second observation to fill its slot, raised the baseline median to 630 and incorrectly established recovery.

resolution.cause: The diagnosed recent window was linked to the issue, while its preceding baseline window was reconstructed from whatever observations still existed.
resolution.correction: Expose the three original baseline report identities for sustained growth and bind them in verification_budget.growth_baseline. Require those exact reports before computing a recovery median and keep their identity in the feedback receipt fingerprint.
resolution.prevention: Remove the original 600-second sample while retaining an earlier 630-second sample. Verify that its exact locator is unavailable and recovery stays pending. Restore the original evidence and exercise both the slower and restored post-correction median.

items.observation: The authenticated workflow failure was written independently and the live status stayed pending. With twelve newer ordinary runs, the first offline reread aged that failure record out of the recent window even though an auxiliary archive still supplied the conflicting older 720-second success. Busy capture and unavailable capture both reproduced the false recovery.

resolution.cause: Failure authority used the same recent-run limit as ordinary captures even when an auxiliary archive still retained the stale success.
resolution.correction: Keep ordinary capture scans bounded and read retained failure authority for the exact ordinary successful attempt identities admitted from auxiliary evidence.
resolution.prevention: Exercise busy and unavailable capture followed immediately by offline reread while twelve newer cold runs remain present. Preserve a separate successful identity and its qualifying elapsed measurement.

items.observation: Main 45407009232 passed in 1192 seconds. Its Python producer alone ended at second 961 with 641.344 seconds of Python and 136.750 seconds of market recovery. Parallel PR 45407157664 passed in 905 seconds with Python last, split between 543.906 and 118.046 seconds. The subsequent seeded full main still had Python running at the 900-second boundary after the other producers succeeded.

resolution.cause: The full Windows Python producer serialized Python contracts and market recovery. The seeded main still took 1011 seconds with the Python producer last after the cache-save work had gone away.
resolution.correction: Run the two original selected commands through the existing bounded overlap runner only in the full Windows Python producer when both are selected and have their ordinary isolated prerequisites. Retain the commands, deadlines, logs, and artifacts.
resolution.prevention: Retain the exact lane-admission regression and the cold-seed and warm-main scheduling observations. Require the actual protected full PR timing and the native Windows interruption result before integration. M0-091 retains the ordinary main budget measurement.

items.source: Real bounded Linux interruption in archives/observations/m0-091-python-lane/local-80301fc/bounded-cancel-market-only/observation.json and bounded-cancel-overlapped/observation.json in the same parent directory.
items.observation: Interrupting the ordinary standalone market-recovery command left its Vite listener and descendants alive in separate POSIX process groups. A paired overlap reproduced the issue while both command reports recorded interrupted and 34 simultaneous observations showed separate writable paths. Probe-owned leftovers were identified by their run directory and explicitly reaped. Windows uses a separate Job Object path, which this observation did not exercise.

resolution.cause: The real Linux Playwright and package launcher descendants left the original process group, so stopping that group left the Vite listener behind on both serial and overlapping runs.
resolution.correction: Enable explicit Linux ownership for market recovery under a dedicated subreaper and reap the owned descendants independently of their process groups.
resolution.prevention: Interrupt the real serial and overlapped market commands after the listener and bridge start. Verify that owned processes exit and the ports release while the unrelated control remains live. Preserve the passing named Chromium control and the exact process observations.

items.source: Independent Standard Astra review of 582404ab1eb0e4e935d42a305cb16e7380da6b6b over M0-092 intake 1d4c587.
items.observation: When market recovery finished first, the main thread blocked in the unbounded Python future wait. A pending interrupt was only serviced after the Python worker exited, and the resulting interruption lost both terminal rows. A completed recovery log and the still-running Python listener must be handled independently of their completion order.

resolution.cause: After market recovery passed first, an unbounded future wait delayed the main-thread interrupt handler until Python exited and allowed KeyboardInterrupt to discard both terminal rows.
resolution.correction: Service the main-thread signal handler with the same bounded future wait in both the normal and interruption paths. Leave each command deadline and terminal result intact.
resolution.prevention: Exercise both first-finisher orders with real listening processes. Require the first row to remain passed, the interrupted row to remain failed with its reason, the listener to release, and both transcript rows and original log digests to survive. Native Windows Job Object coverage remains an exact PR gate.

items.observation: The real process-group SIGTERM also terminated the Linux supervisor. The check returned cleanup_failed and an owned detached child remained alive after return. The direct-command termination control preserved -15.

resolution.cause: The contained command shared its process group with the Linux supervisor. A group SIGTERM killed the supervisor with its command and left an owned detached descendant alive.
resolution.correction: Start the command in its own process session so group termination reaches the command and leaves the supervisor running to reap the owned process tree.
resolution.prevention: Exercise real group SIGTERM and the direct-command control, retain the actual -15 exit, and verify that the owned detached descendant is gone and the unrelated control survives. Keep the independent t104 red and approved correction evidence.

items.observation: The same command exited explicitly with status 7 under both environments. A supervisor inheriting SIGCHLD ignored reported exit 0 instead of 7, and automatic reaping invalidated the held-child identity premise.

resolution.cause: Inherited ignored SIGCHLD made Linux automatically reap the command before the supervisor collected the original status. The same ordinary exit 7 was reported as exit 0.
resolution.correction: Restore the default SIGCHLD disposition in the isolated supervisor before launching the command so it can collect the original exit and preserve owned identities through cleanup.
resolution.prevention: Use matching real commands with default and inherited ignored SIGCHLD. Require both explicit failures to retain exit 7 and keep the separate success and cancellation observations. Retain t104 review and regression records.

resolution.cause: The Rust registry verified the saved connection only before the worker awaited the HTTP reply. The dialogue then accepted a result with the original request ID even after a peer had replaced the saved settings.
resolution.correction: Recheck the saved connection ID, origin and rule version in the profile-bound registry before handing the sample to the UI. Reject a superseded trial with STALE_CONTEXT.
resolution.prevention: Hold the real reply while a second native bridge replaces the connection in the same SQLite profile. Release the reply, require STALE_CONTEXT and no displayed sample, and verify the request count is unchanged while loading the newer settings. The independent Astra review at d5e3aad identified two existing tests that still expected a blank editor on ordinary reopen. Preserve the covered candle replay stop and first-open blank behaviors while updating the reopen outcomes.

resolution.cause: The removable dialog owned the accepted temporary workbench and selection. Ordinary close unmounted the owner.
resolution.correction: Keep the accepted prototype definition and selection with the desktop window session and restore them when the dialog opens again. Draft text, preview selection and replay execution remain dialog-local.
resolution.prevention: Verify the first blank canvas, accepted same-window reopen, usable restored selection, discarded preview and rejected draft, fresh blank session and stopped candle replay in the existing renderer interaction check. Exercise the same-window accepted restore through real WebView2 UI Automation.

Legitimate admission refusals can also reuse the original request ID before the loss.

items.observation: The full window succeeded. On the second cropped click the browser recorded net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET at 116 ms for indicator.createDraft d257b5d7-58c9-43a0-993b-29d265950cb7. The failure preceded any observed runPreview or status and lost was empty. The historical trace does not show whether the server received the command. Same-run Linux and the prior passing Windows run show createDraft receiving 429 BUSY while an old task.cancel finishes, then admitting the same request ID. The older M0-099 Windows failure still has no known underlying reply.

resolution.cause: The original browser observed a connection reset at draft delivery. The collector did not establish whether the Windows writer received or committed it. Real same-source overlap controls returned pre-admission BUSY, and an owned transport probe exposed premature shutdown on that verified branch.
resolution.correction: Deliver the already-decided BUSY after completing bounded intake of the authorized request body. Keep explicit pre-admission retries and the existing draft identity. Avoid automatic replay of an ambiguous mutation.

Keep the full and cropped zero, warmup, M0-099 status recovery, terminal case and cancellation. Review and logs are indexed at archives/observations/m0-101-draft-delivery/index.json.

items.source: Independent real Vite and Rust writer transport probe on f52ce52449124729601908b58c2e0477af26a6fe. Retained archives/observations/m0-101-draft-delivery/base.ndjson SHA-256 42d22406f4182e729ec91d3a65c6da6e6134890767742fe7596602edbf84342f and drain.ndjson SHA-256 0d43988961a79a7512a8bd79f33178c172f687c7d33eaec326b9fa75d5064e39.
items.observation: With an admitted cancellation waiting for its real writer reply, the HTTP pre-admission BUSY response finished before the competing authenticated POST was complete and destroyed its request socket. This occurred on a reused socket, a fresh socket, and a split body. The bounded drain control finished only with the request complete and socket alive, with no competing bytes sent to the writer. Linux clients decoded BUSY on both paths, so the controlled defect does not prove the recorded hosted Windows connection reset mechanism.

resolution.cause: The authorized early BUSY path generated its response before consuming the body. The shared failure response closed the connection with an incomplete request and its request-destroy callback ran in the controlled baseline.
resolution.correction: Stream-discard the already-refused authorized body under the existing byte and time bounds. Send structured BUSY only on complete intake and leave the writer lane available.
resolution.prevention: Reproduce premature headers and socket destruction before correction. Verify after correction that both complete refusals return 429. Witness a real committed draft, discard the caller response, explicitly resend the exact command in the test and compare its receipt. Reject different content under the same key and preserve the original receipt. The real transport controls and t9p approval are retained at archives/observations/m0-101-draft-delivery/index.json.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard review of c3e616a7c5b8f11edeea7c5f4e0fc83e64746886. Retained at archives/observations/m0-102-profile-pool/astra-c3e616a.txt.
items.observation: The browser fixture external deadline terminates the directly started workspace bridge. Its ten-second PowerShell deadline starts after spawning the helper, so the outer deadline can win before bridge-driven cleanup. Setup then removes the pool even when the PowerShell descendant may still write. The existing controlled test only exercised a direct process.

resolution.cause: The original outer timeout terminated the directly launched bridge. A PowerShell descendant could still write after the fixture removed its pool.
resolution.correction: Use the owned process supervisor for the bridge and its descendants. Confirm the tree stopped before removing the pool and retain the pool when that cannot be confirmed.
resolution.prevention: Keep the active grandchild timeout and unconfirmed-cleanup regressions in python-contracts-workers and the ordinary workspace-timeframe entry. The original red and corrected controls are retained in archives/observations/m0-102-profile-pool/index.json.

items.observation: Moving the preparation timeout into the owned Python supervisor fixed the descendant cleanup race. The caller now waits without a startup bound before the interpreter can enforce the supplied deadline. A stalled startup has no prompt reply or verified handoff.

resolution.cause: The first supervisor implementation could wait for interpreter startup before it began to enforce the operation deadline.
resolution.correction: Start the twelve-second caller budget before spawning the supervisor. Require a ready signal and an explicit grant before the supervisor acquires a pool or starts the bridge, then enforce the remaining budget through the owned process tree.
resolution.prevention: Keep the absent and expired grant regressions and the controlled pre-readiness and launched-descendant deadline observations. Their source and results are retained in archives/observations/m0-102-profile-pool/index.json.

items.source: Windows and Linux M0-102 task verification 45478673119 attempt 1 at f5bb2aeeebfc3964b420a9ffef8cc459c7f1f5bb.
