The exact CPython 3.12.10 Windows mkdir implementation is https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.10/Modules/posixmodule.c#L5022-L5046.
items.observation: The ordinary Windows browser global setup returned prepare/replaceable-ancestor after 375 ms and ran zero scenarios. Rust batch preparation, profile isolation and broad-access refusal passed there, as did the Python descendant supervision tests and the Linux task. The browser supervisor creates its exclusive outer directory using Python mode 0700; the passing Rust Windows process fixture uses default inherited creation. The tagged CPython source emits a full-access Owner Rights ACE for that special mode, which meets the current ancestor refusal predicate. The original Windows report lacks the literal rejected path component and ACE.

resolution.cause: The browser supervisor used CPython Windows mkdir mode 0700 for its synthetic outer directory. CPython 3.12.10 creates a full-access Owner Rights ACE for that mode, which matches the existing ancestor refusal. The hosted failure did not log the specific rejected path component or ACE.
resolution.correction: Create the exclusive Windows scratch directory with its native inherited ACL. The unchanged storage helper creates and checks the privately owned roots below it. POSIX continues to use mode 0700.
resolution.prevention: Exercise the actual Windows temporary parent through the ordinary browser suite. Open a privately prepared root through the normal writer, refuse the CPython 0700 and Everyone DeleteChild ancestors, and verify neither refused pool remains. Run 45484754044 supplies the native result.

items.observation: The native ancestor regression asserted its positive profile came from the shared pool after calling a helper that legitimately falls back to single preparation after sixty-four claims. A repeated or bigger run could fail before the real writer and negative cases.

resolution.cause: The positive control took a slot from the ordinary browser pool and asserted that a fallback profile still belonged to that pool.
resolution.correction: Give the control a separate one-profile pool under the same temporary parent. Require that exact slot to open with the ordinary writer.
resolution.prevention: Keep the pool-capacity red and isolated-control green in archives/observations/m0-102-native-correction/index.json and the same-parent native browser control in workspace-timeframe.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard review of f6625175407eb511dadca66dd83a58a0dbe7b854. Retained at archives/observations/m0-102-native-correction/astra-f662517.txt.
items.observation: The original-mode control recorded the directory only after the Python child successfully returned its marker. If the directory was created and the result was lost, teardown did not own or remove it. The production scratch and protected child ACL policy have no finding in this review.

resolution.cause: The first native control learned the synthetic 0700 directory from the Python child's success marker. Directory creation followed by a lost result could leave the directory outside teardown ownership.
resolution.correction: Own the enclosing control directory before invoking the child and keep all of its paths beneath it. Remove the enclosing directory after confirming pending pools no longer exist.
resolution.prevention: Keep the controlled lost-result cleanup evidence in archives/observations/m0-102-native-correction/index.json and exercise the enclosing teardown in the ordinary Windows browser control.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard early source review of M0-105 at intake 8206dd8b450da3935965b86dab25ab8cf884140e. Retained at archives/observations/m0-105-native-workspace-acl/astra-early-design-8206dd8.txt.
items.observation: The Windows libtest draft registered its ACL worker only in Profile::new. The original writer and decision-note restoration interruption fixtures start fresh libtest processes and call support::store directly, so their ordinary open would use the executable worker arguments with no libtest entry selected.

resolution.cause: Fresh libtest processes entering support::store directly missed the ACL worker registration installed by the profile fixture.
resolution.correction: Register the test worker at the direct store entry so the fresh processes resolve the Windows ACL worker through the ordinary writer path.
resolution.prevention: The Rust suite exercises interrupted writer and decision-note restore before commit in fresh processes. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard early source review of M0-105 at intake 8206dd8b450da3935965b86dab25ab8cf884140e. Retained at archives/observations/m0-105-native-workspace-acl/astra-early-design-8206dd8.txt.
items.observation: The native draft called Job::new and Command::spawn synchronously, and captured no entry-through-ready duration. The desktop has no Node startup fence. The caller therefore could not withdraw authorization and return by its existing admission deadline while cold launch remained in flight.

resolution.cause: Synchronous Job and child startup could outlast the caller before it could withdraw authority.
resolution.correction: Bound the caller wait through launch and worker readiness. Only a ready worker holding caller authorization can proceed, and the owned launch path cleans up an abandoned worker.
resolution.prevention: The Rust cold-launch test exercises withdrawal before readiness and rejects a late grant. Hosted workspace and desktop transport also exercise ordinary admission. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

items.source: Independent Windows ACL semantic review of commit 5c655b5801fe92eee3017f9fca0e033288443e9f, windows.rs blob f6c1075bc479368c069cd12e8bbc2112f5ce318f. items.observation: The native draft validated a drive, then reinterpreted the validated path components as new paths while assembling each ancestor. The source allows the resolved path to leave the checked ancestor chain. No unsafe hosted access was observed.

resolution.cause: Rebuilding Windows paths could reinterpret a component outside the previously checked drive and ancestor chain.
resolution.correction: Construct the chain only from validated ordinary components on one drive and keep the checked ancestor handles through admission.
resolution.prevention: The Rust path-chain regression checks drive confinement and rejection of ambiguous names. Native ancestor and ordinary workspace checks exercise admission and refusal. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

items.source: Independent Windows ACL semantic review of commit 5c655b5801fe92eee3017f9fca0e033288443e9f, windows.rs blob f6c1075bc479368c069cd12e8bbc2112f5ce318f. Original at archives/observations/m0-105-native-workspace-acl/specialist-windows-acl-5c655b5.txt (SHA-256 4bb21216db961cca4124e390ad5f74c3ef1de1e8277ebb1267f7117a48fcccc6).
items.observation: The native draft called GetLengthSid on an ACE SID before validating the SID and the full bounded representation. The query requires a valid SID. No malformed NTFS descriptor was observed.

resolution.cause: The draft passed an unbounded, unvalidated ACE SID to a Win32 length routine that requires a valid SID.
resolution.correction: Bound the SID header and subauthority extent by the enclosing ACE before native validation and use.
resolution.prevention: The Rust SID header and subauthority regression and malformed ACE tests cover rejection before normalization. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

items.source: Independent Windows ACL semantic review of commit 5c655b5801fe92eee3017f9fca0e033288443e9f, windows.rs blob f6c1075bc479368c069cd12e8bbc2112f5ce318f. Original at archives/observations/m0-105-native-workspace-acl/specialist-windows-acl-5c655b5.txt (SHA-256 4bb21216db961cca4124e390ad5f74c3ef1de1e8277ebb1267f7117a48fcccc6). The coordinator retained two narrow source approvals of 0d0495b8e953cb41f4cb1dcef497e220374c7b91 and the ordered-rule red and green probe artifacts in archives/observations/m0-105-native-workspace-acl/index-0d0495.json (SHA-256 543ae7cbdf91a1b19ec272e43b809483d159119f745dcf6866745c543e89dd91). The index records that the standalone approval transcripts were unavailable.
items.observation: The managed ACL reader can compact ordinary equivalent explicit rules before the former inheritance predicate. The native draft applies that predicate to raw individual rules. Native compatibility for split same-user inheritance grants needs a differential check. The two-ACE limit rejects a canonical same-user group where any two of three equal-scope grants supply full control. The equal-flags requirement also rejects same-user full control split into separately representable child object and child container scopes. These are source-review findings and require the normal Windows comparison. A canonical private ACL can still pass the prior ordered adjacent compaction even when not every two rules cover full control. The four-rule review example necessarily has a full compacted pair. Preserve the actual same-principal sort and one-pass compaction across ordinary rule counts, including order-dependent refusal. The integrated source still folds a merged pair into subsequent ACEs and discards an already complete inherited grant. The two exact-source controls in .reports/m0-105-compatibility/red.log observed an incorrect admit and refusal. The historical DirectorySecurity export normalizes once, while the candidate differential applied a second normalization. Microsoft .NET Framework reference source: https://github.com/microsoft/referencesource/blob/main/mscorlib/system/security/accesscontrol/acl.cs#L1144-L1181 and https://github.com/microsoft/referencesource/blob/main/mscorlib/system/security/accesscontrol/nativeobjectsecurity.cs#L157.

resolution.cause: Raw ACE checks and repeated folding diverged from the managed export order and one-pass adjacent compaction, including complete inherited grants.
resolution.correction: Preserve the managed same-principal order and apply adjacent compaction once before the private access predicate. The differential consumes the baseline managed export once.
resolution.prevention: The Windows Rust regressions check principal order, inherited grants and both the allowed and refused managed-layout outcomes through native admission. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard exact review of 4411815c5f24f927b8f8a44dda96fbc7bf474c4e. Original at archives/observations/m0-105-native-workspace-acl/astra-4411815.txt (SHA-256 ffb83e69eb9d48bfd3f64428f3d265eb23e1e10e7717661a065bfeb02da5579a).
items.observation: The post-grant timeout test immediately checked for no late marker after releasing its worker. That observation can occur before a still-running worker polls again. Preserve the actual worker handle and require it to be signaled when the supervisor returns.

resolution.cause: The immediate marker check could succeed before a still-running worker had another opportunity to write.
resolution.correction: Retain the exact worker process handle and require it to be signaled when the supervisor returns after timeout.
resolution.prevention: The Rust timed-out worker regression verifies process exit at return. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

items.source: Astra Standard source review of PR 84 head d9102de9c036fb6ae4b962a5dfa9529927110315 against protected main 9180963fb3185dbceaafcaf19ee5f2dc78ae3649. Original copy .reports/m0-105-file-ace/astra-pr84-d9102de.txt (SHA-256 dc41ecc5c1c497bf50791f78d36611921e74a2f1fda5011564882655e4e199dc). Microsoft .NET Framework InspectAce: https://github.com/microsoft/referencesource/blob/main/mscorlib/system/security/accesscontrol/acl.cs#L1008-L1073.
items.observation: The reviewed native path refused a foreign SID before filtering an ordinary ACE with no granted rights. It also treated inheritance flags as meaningful on a regular file. The historical managed ACL export drops zero masks and leaf inherit-only entries, while a directory inherit-only grant with object or container inheritance still comes under the private-principal policy. This is a source-confirmed compatibility defect. The passing Windows run for d9102de did not exercise these descriptors.

resolution.cause: The first native predicate rejected foreign principals and file inheritance flags before the managed inert-entry filtering.
resolution.correction: Validate first, then discard zero-mask entries and regular-file inherit-only entries before access evaluation. Keep applicable directory inheritance and actual file grants under the private principal rule.
resolution.prevention: The Windows Rust differential runs same-user reopen and rejected sharing through ordinary admission and verifies byte-identical DB and WAL after refusal. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

items.observation: Two ordinary Linux workspace journeys received TIMEOUT from instrument.search. The desktop chart-opened snapshot received BUSY after the frozen-chart reply showed opened. The Linux browser paths are independent of the Windows ACL worker. All three matching cases passed sequentially on the same Linux browser and service code with isolated loopback ports, one Playwright worker and the original deadlines. This establishes a nonrecurrence in isolation. The original run did not attribute the TIMEOUT to a particular worker phase or identify the other request occupying admission when the snapshot returned BUSY. The completed follow-up used separate loopback listeners and the existing deadlines. The isolated one-worker baseline passed 2 workspace cases and 1 desktop case. Each of three ordinary sequential check pairs passed all 59 workspace cases with 2 workers and all 8 desktop cases with 1 worker. That is 204 case executions and 12 of 12 matched passes, with zero failures, skips or flaky results. The scoped attachments recorded 44 distinct instrument.search requests with zero TIMEOUT and four successful chart-opened snapshots with zero unexpected BUSY. The held-reader controls returned the eight expected scripted BUSY replies, one snapshot and one frozen-chart request per round. All eight check process trees terminated, four workspace setup directories and seven desktop profile directories were cleared, all eight owned temporary directories were removed, and no observed listener remained. The two original search failures were admitted by the preview and returned TIMEOUT in an HTTP 200 body. The original worker phase and the operation holding desktop admission remain unknown. At the next ordinary Linux recurrence in either linked check, the verification owner of that run takes M0-119 and retains the failing raw report and scoped attachments before any retry. For search TIMEOUT, correlate the preview request and Rust bridge with worker launch, hello, request send and terminal reply, recording the last completed phase and elapsed times. For an unexpected chart-opened BUSY, correlate the refused snapshot with the operation type and request identity holding admission when the refusal occurred, including whether it is the scripted held reader. Record worker count, existing deadlines and a same-source ordinary control. Retain the traces with the original failure and assign a bounded corrective task to the entry point that owns the observed stage once it is identified.

items.observation: The native DACL type dispatch refused structurally valid common callback entries before applying the object-specific normalization. The managed descriptor discarded a zero-mask callback on a directory and an inherit-only callback on a regular file before the storage policy rejected remaining callbacks. The managed comparison also skipped effective callbacks instead of refusing them. The review confirmed the difference in source. It did not observe these descriptors on a Windows run.

resolution.cause: Type dispatch rejected inert common callback layouts before the managed object-specific filtering, while the comparison skipped effective callbacks.
resolution.correction: Decode and bound known callback layouts before inert-entry filtering and reject any unsupported callback that survives. Align the managed differential with that rejection stage.
resolution.prevention: The Windows Rust layout and managed access regressions cover inert and effective common callbacks on files and directories, including malformed bounds. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

items.observation: The native decoder refused ObjectAce layouts before the managed baseline would remove inert known entries. The existing negative test changed a common ACE type without adding object flags and optional GUIDs, so it represented a malformed object buffer. Reference-source review also identified the legacy CompoundAce known layout and the distinct opaque CustomAce envelope. No NTFS outcome for these added cases was observed in the source review.

resolution.cause: The draft rejected valid object layouts before inert-entry filtering, and its type-byte mutation did not construct a valid object ACE.
resolution.correction: Decode recognized ObjectAce, object callback and CompoundAce layouts with their own bounds before applying inert-entry rules. Keep surviving unsupported grants and unknown layouts refused.
resolution.prevention: Windows Rust covers all four object GUID-presence combinations and malformed or unknown controls. The managed differential exercises structurally valid directory and file entries and verifies ordinary reopen and byte-stable refusal. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

items.observation: The bounded native decoder accepted trailing data past the managed layout-specific limit and could discard such an entry as inert. In the managed path construction of the qualified ACE rejects that length before DACL normalization, even when its access mask is zero. The exact aligned maxima are 65456 bytes for CommonAce and 65420 for ObjectAce with either callback setting. This is a source-confirmed difference pending native execution.

resolution.cause: An oversized opaque tail could pass structural decoding and disappear as inert before the historical managed limit was applied.
resolution.correction: Enforce the layout-specific CommonAce and ObjectAce opaque-length limits before Ace normalization, for ordinary and callback shapes.
resolution.prevention: The Windows Rust opaque-length regression tests the aligned maxima and the first aligned lengths above them. The ordinary Windows storage differential exercises private-workspace compatibility and byte-stable refusal. Official Windows run 45556094486 recorded this regression in project/evidence/M0-105-1441cab6f7c78975.json.

The controlled two-tab Chromium run first delayed approval until a peer committed 5m. Approval returned STALE_CONTEXT, the note and outcome remained and no success appeared. A newly reviewed approval then returned a matching non-undoable receipt. SQLite contained the deletion marker at the committed revision and neither the note nor its outcome. The held list reply contained no notes and the peer displayed the empty list. The initiating tab showed success while that reply was delayed, then removed it when the list response was lost. Both existing peer scenarios passed in that run. The exact operation outcome and refresh ordering in the original hosted failure remain unknown.

resolution.cause: In controlled Linux Chromium, the deletion had a verified receipt, then a lost list response cleared the selection and its already-confirmed action notice together. The original hosted operation outcome and ordering were not captured.
resolution.correction: Retain the confirmed deletion notice while refreshing or recovering the list. A failed post-commit list read reports its own error and exposes the existing reload action. A rejected or unverified approval cannot set the deletion notice.
resolution.prevention: The two-tab Chromium control verifies peer STALE_CONTEXT refusal and intact rows, then a matching committed receipt, removal of note and outcome, a revision-bound deletion marker and a peer empty list. Dropping the initiating list response retains success through the explicit reload. The ordinary draft, consent and peer removal assertions are still checked. The positive observation is in archives/observations/m2-036-note-deletion-74103f6/observed-deletion.json (SHA-256 7b384646ae7d1e6905711fa60d776455e76c4d4dde36a81a669bb86eef7d62fe).

items.observation: After one confirmed deletion, the first lost list response produced the list-refresh alert and retained success. A second lost list response from Reload decision notes replaced the refresh alert with The local workspace could not verify the result. The deletion was already verified and no additional deletion request was sent. A successful list read should clear the list alert and retain the confirmed result. The real two-tab Linux control reproduced both list alerts in that order. All three reads returned an empty list from the server, the first two replies were lost, and the third reached the browser. There was one successful-phase approval request, and the deletion marker and missing rows were identical before and after retries. The peer displayed the empty list without the initiating tab notice.

resolution.cause: Reload decision notes used the operation failure descriptor after the post-commit list refresh had already established a separate read failure.
resolution.correction: Use the same list refresh descriptor for an explicit list retry after a verified deletion. Keep the existing note target and operation failure descriptor for detail retries and unverified outcomes.
resolution.prevention: Real Chromium received two list-specific alerts after two lost replies. The third read cleared the list alert, the initiating success and peer empty list persisted, and only one successful-phase approval was sent with the durable rows unchanged by retries. The known cancellation and unknown-result controls passed. items.observation: After the list recovered following a confirmed deletion, opening New decision note left the old Decision note deleted. status visible in the new editor. It remained until draft review. Opening an editor starts a new action, so retire the earlier notice at that user gesture while read-only retries retain it. No extra approved delete was sent and the stored deletion marker remained identical.

resolution.cause: The new-note button opened its editor without clearing the previous action notice.
resolution.correction: Clear the old notice when the user starts a new note. Keep the current notice during read-only recovery.
resolution.prevention: The real Chromium case retains success until the new-note gesture, then observes the editor without the earlier delete notice. items.observation: The report inspected 88 registered worktrees. The consumer scans for audit-windows-acl, series-frame-probe and workbench-runtime-verification exceeded the fixed 20,000-entry budget. Those three incomplete observations produced a shared consumer hold across all rows. The snapshot also reported separate process visibility, registration and recovery reference holds.

resolution.cause: The fixed per-checkout ignored-path traversal budget interrupted a consumer scan in each of the three large checkouts.
resolution.correction: Expose a validated entry limit on the existing retirement command and use it in the ignored-path inventories and Python consumer directories. Preserve the exhaustion hold.
resolution.prevention: A native Git fixture reaches a real nested link with an explicit 20,001-entry budget and confirms the unchanged default still reports exhaustion. The required checks passed on d2c15146bb2f8c3606f4df3e12fca469d775f9b7.

items.source: Astra Standard independent review of 10bd459fae00e67c3f8d7ae0b3b7ef860351d22a on 2026-11-25.
items.observation: With an observation limit of one, the initial ignored-root sort still consumes a synthetic list of 10,000 sibling names before enforcing the budget. Git status also materializes the complete ignored root list before the traversal. Dirty status and status process failures must still be observed after limiting retained ignored paths.

resolution.cause: Status parsing decoded all ignored roots, and the initial path sort evaluated the entire iterable before the inspection counter took effect.
resolution.correction: Stream Git status and retain up to the budget plus one root as an overflow witness. Bound the initial traversal intake before sorting and verify Git completion while preserving dirty status.
resolution.prevention: A real 64-root Git fixture with a dirty tracked file measures two retained roots with a budget of one. Additional regressions measure the initial iterator and exercise a native rename whose source begins with an ignored-status prefix. The pre-fix regression log is retained at .reports/audit-20261125/retirement-root-intake-red.log with SHA-256 f4e4c66619ab3dbe3b469437d91af1923bc37af9ca5dea9e7912ba0e204f1228. items.source: Second Astra Standard independent review of 95f20e913f2d4d91f347156af10d72467b4b3f74 on 2026-11-25.
items.observation: At an entry limit of one, a stream with 10,000 ignored roots and a tracked modification at the tail yielded 10,001 records and 158,901 bytes to the consumer. The operation classified the checkout as dirty and retained two ignored paths, while continuing to consume the entire ignored listing after overflow was known.

resolution.cause: The ignored collector kept reading Git stdout after overflow to find ordinary dirty records and determine the final process status.
resolution.correction: Observe ordinary Git status independently. Stop the ignored stream after one excess root, preserve any already observed Git failure, and close and reap the producer.
resolution.prevention: The measured native Git fixture reduced ignored stdout consumption from 2,048 records and 165,888 bytes to two records and 4,096 bytes. Separate regressions cover tail dirtiness, nonzero exits before and at overflow, an unreadable pipe, child cleanup and complete small trees. The original regression log is retained at .reports/audit-20261125/m0-116-red.log with SHA-256 1ac03d8cccb3442841c31fa74ed607f675e0c8b193664f88ed8b1c30906cb001.

items.observation: The first ordinary status query was empty and the second query read a change to a tracked file or an ordinary untracked path. The retirement result nevertheless reported clean true, zero holds, and candidate because the second status query discarded ordinary observations it actually read.

resolution.correction: Keep the dirty flag true once either query has observed an ordinary record. Preserve the ignored budget cutoff, error holds, and process cleanup.
resolution.prevention: Both native Git regressions reproduced an eligible dirty checkout before the fix. items.observation: The obsolete-input browser case failed when its direct indicator_preview_status response body reported BUSY instead of STALE_CONTEXT after the cancel exchange. The probe discarded HTTP status and did not record the competing request or registry stage. Windows passed on the same preview checkout. The ordinary product already polls BUSY within its existing deadline. The failing assertion was in the one-shot test probe, and its original BUSY stage remains unknown. In the controlled Chromium red, the original held ready request settled after invalidation, with acceptance absent. A separately tagged snapshot reached the actual Rust writer. The obsolete status probe against that holder returned HTTP 429 with retryable BUSY, and the matching writer reply drained at revision 1. Treating this refusal as the semantic answer reproduced the assertion failure.

resolution.cause: The direct test probed obsolete status once and discarded HTTP status. In Chromium a separately tagged Rust snapshot held the writer, and the probe was refused with HTTP 429 before the stale check; the original hosted holder and stage were unobserved.
resolution.correction: Use one bounded read-only probe which retries only an explicit retryable HTTP 429 BUSY. Keep admitted replies, the expected STALE_CONTEXT, mutation and UI assertions, and exact output comparison.
resolution.prevention: The real control observes a cancelled late browser delivery, a still-held snapshot and one refused read stopped by caller cancellation. A subsequent read receives 429, the exact snapshot drains, and the same task returns HTTP 200 STALE_CONTEXT. Stale mutations are refused and the earlier document is identical after restart. The outcome is retained at archives/observations/m0-122-obsolete-indicator-status-green-5b66ac2/observed-status.json (SHA-256 f04d68833b21c2cc1a1fd00f952018ec2613bc94d86ea162845a830afd4f9a8c).

items.observation: Injected route.fulfill threw the original error and disposed the fetched response, but the awaiting test still waited for forwarded. The worker could interrupt the test before the route, service and profile followed their owning finally blocks. Forwarding and the intercepted browser request completion share a finite verification window. The local replay observed the exact injected error and disposed response with the original forwarding waiter pending.

resolution.cause: Only successful forwarding settled the deferred result. A thrown route error disposed the response but left the test waiting.
resolution.correction: Settle the captured forwarding result on success or failure and keep the original failure through disposal. Use one bound for forwarding and captured request completion. Distinguish an already cancelled Chromium request from an ordinary missing response.
resolution.prevention: Inject the original error into a live Chromium route and an independent absent response. Verify exact error identity, removal of the owned route, release of the listener and profile removal. The ordinary workflow observes genuine cancellation. Reserve the port before preparing the profile and verify the real profile still closes after a later failure. resolution.correction: Reserve the loopback port before acquiring the profile; keep the existing owning finally for later failures.

items.observation: Repeated retryable 429 BUSY responses exhausted the probe timeout with only a boolean poll assertion. Both obsolete status and shared accepted-output probes need attempted request count and the last numeric HTTP status, BUSY code and retryability without response body or capability text. The local replay observed three retryable 429 attempts and verified the old diagnostic did not identify HTTP 429 or code BUSY.

resolution.cause: The former boolean poll assertion retained no transport fields when the admission budget expired.
resolution.correction: Keep the original absolute deadline and retry only the supported retryable HTTP 429 BUSY envelope. At expiry report the attempted count and last validated refusal fields. Preserve caller cancellation and return every other response to the assertion.
resolution.prevention: The shared accepted-output probe sees repeated real HTTP 429 while the Rust snapshot stays held. Its bounded failure records the attempt count, HTTP 429, BUSY and retryability. The stale and malformed requests are returned after one attempt each; cancellation and reopened output are still checked. See archives/observations/m0-123-indicator-fixture/green-75aca56/observed.json (SHA-256 1fc528499e2d229bf4e6edb314091c0581fcfb11e6de377fecda04bb7c19d1b3).

items.source: Astra Standard repeat review of M0-123 source 75aca5612da59e6c4b415aee0e7b64edfff9171f, archives/observations/m0-124-indicator-observer/astra-m0-123-75aca56.txt (SHA-256 6924986d05b324f36249808fff84a530af3149bed1fe2616795925f10e7b21e1). Exact-base fixture regression at 2b20311687f1fabf734e5381fa48309c975e1d42: archives/observations/m0-124-indicator-observer/red-2b20311/SHA256SUMS (SHA-256 280d5864c42fd3b43e6d1173b9965d61e46c400cbfbd8164109d356c3fd414c7) and observed.json (SHA-256 bc5e9abd5415e6df7f73b964c7e53ac9cc5ee51f9cc7c7584e9949a60d9bcbfa).
items.observation: The actual probe awaited its undo observer after the first retryable HTTP 429. That callback started a separate 3-second drained wait. A drain after the read deadline settled in 3.807 seconds, and withholding drain settled in 4.206 seconds with an AbortError that omitted the refusal. An explicit caller cancellation at 161 milliseconds returned only at 813 milliseconds. The controls must separate deadline with late or withheld drain from early caller cancellation, and prove that admitted and nonretryable replies and arbitrary observer errors remain intact. With a 500 ms read budget the late case took 1013 ms and completed the wait after the late notification. The missing event took 3015 ms and lost the refusal. The explicit cancellation took 3016 ms and lost the original reason. The admitted and nonretryable controls each returned after one request. An unrelated observer error with the caller reason as its cause was replaced by that reason.

resolution.cause: The read probe started a single timeout, but the observer callback awaited an independent drained timeout. Its generic cause check could also turn an unrelated observer error into cancellation.
resolution.correction: Pass the composed read signal into both real drain observers and the snapshot wait. Abort removes pending event subscriptions. Preserve the original reason of a caller abort and report the captured refusal on the internal deadline. Propagate other observer failures.
resolution.prevention: The controlled loopback probe exercises late and withheld IPC, early caller cancellation, admitted and nonretryable replies, and an unrelated error sharing the caller abort as its cause. Each makes one request. In the two deadline cases the probe reports the retained HTTP 429 BUSY retryable fields. All three drain waiters clean their listeners. Exact source evidence: archives/observations/m0-124-indicator-observer/green-58191c3/observed.json (SHA-256 8f7e3598cdbb6e321334bab5e8df343775339dbce0585dc327a18a46770d4895).

items.observation: The first private-handoff assertion at workspace.spec.mjs:3404 failed with only PowerShell execution. The probe did not retain the stage for startup, timeout, signal, buffer limit or an undeclared nonzero exit. The archived failure does not identify which disposition occurred.

resolution.cause: The earlier wrapper collapsed undeclared subprocess failures into the generic PowerShell execution label. The condition that caused the original Windows subprocess to fail remains unclassified.
resolution.correction: Expose a bounded startup, deadline, signal, output limit or exit disposition from the test-owned runner while retaining the existing native ACL assertions and limits.
resolution.prevention: Guarded native Windows run 45585469848 passed the private handoff ACL assertion, both unsafe fixtures and the profile pool ACL case. If the failure recurs during ordinary Windows verification, retain the exact source, raw report and bound log with the last safe stage and observed subprocess disposition before any retry. Reopen only against that new observation, keeping paths, arguments, SID and stderr out of diagnostics.

items.source: Astra Standard review of 3b1dfe67fb91d2fa264e134e9e8b14f56206b583 and independently repeated Node 24.22.3 child-process observations.
items.observation: With a 400 ms limit and descendant-held output pipes, native execFile returned success at 403 ms and declared exit 58 at 404 ms. The candidate took about 1.35 seconds and mislabelled exit 58 as a deadline. The reviewer also observed a child live after timeout rejection and asynchronous overflow controls that emitted no bytes. Synchronous writes to each output descriptor consistently triggered the output limit.

resolution.cause: The separate abort timer could wait on inherited output after a direct child exited and relabel its existing result. The asynchronous buffer controls did not reliably produce bytes.
resolution.correction: Use Node execFile to bound pipe closure, preserve finished direct-child outcomes and wait for a running child to terminate. Emit overflow bytes synchronously to each descriptor in the test fixtures.
resolution.prevention: The guarded Ubuntu suite passed all eleven subprocess controls. The guarded native Windows suite passed ten applicable controls and named the POSIX child-signal skip separately. The controls cover retained streams after success and a declared exit, reaping at a genuine deadline and both output buffer limits.

items.source: Ordinary offline status at f5bb2aeeebfc3964b420a9ffef8cc459c7f1f5bb and authenticated automatic first-attempt pull requests 45444242059, 45459661035 and 45475965426. items.observation: Three successful comparable ordinary full warm Windows pull requests took 869, 910 and 917 seconds under the 900-second objective. The latter two breach the objective. Each original selected 35 check identities with 28 passes and seven expected unimplemented omissions. The observed runs include both three- and four-producer layouts. This is a new PR recurrence after the repaired PR cohort; the protected main-push finding remains independent.

resolution.cause: The recurrence had two distinct critical paths. The 910-second warm PR waited for browser and the 917-second warm PR waited for Python. The new browser-critical run gained time in setup, chiefly Cargo restore. These observations do not isolate a single cause for both original breaches.
resolution.correction: Qualify the exact protected Windows preparation correction on a natural full warm PR. PR 96 first attempt 45563183277 passed in 876 seconds with the correction in both tested parents and matching outcomes for all 35 selected checks.
resolution.prevention: Keep the digested ordinary PR controls and require exact repair ancestry, complete producer clocks, matching outcomes and full warm cache evidence for any future disposition. The task-bound regression receipt and native provenance are indexed in contracts/reviews/2026-11-25-pr-timing-recurrences.json.

The collector marked the sample complete. It must query current metadata without following reparse points or trusting enumeration sizes for Windows regular file paths.

resolution.correction: For the one-shot probe, query the current logical length through a non-following Windows metadata handle for each regular file path. Preserve alias path accounting and the scan deadline.

PR 112 run 45606747991 attempt 1 retains the native result and logs. The reviewed cleanup removes the diagnostic. Each of the four accepted records scanned target and labeled only git/db as missing. resolution.cause: A rendered citation caption appeared to be authored evidence. Recovery also lacked a route to replace an outstanding request after the source changed.
resolution.correction: Select eligible authored review passages and permit a recorded replacement request bound to its source and predecessor.

resolution.cause: The fixture hashed the original LF string before a text-mode write. Windows saved different bytes and review intake correctly hashed the saved original.

items.source: Linux local M0-147 task run 20261125T181716.486623Z-e13b2103 at 0ff1c4da15fbede912b909aef2ad226ba7fce838. The original is archives/runs/20261125T181716.486623Z-e13b2103/test-report.json. The workspace-timeframe log has SHA-256 2deec7f8863299d655dd7887ecebe5ef22fb3fe358dd5ca6461dcd034394a064.
items.observation: In the paired-window note contention journey the initiator committed one deletion at revision 5 and its same-request list retry changed from HTTP 429 to 200. The observing window saw revision 5, received DATA_UNAVAILABLE for the deleted detail and then received HTTP 429 on its fallback list. It stayed on Reload with the busy notice. The original M2-038 repair covered the initiating list read.

resolution.cause: After a peer deleted the open detail, the observer used a one-shot list read. A temporary refusal left the drawer on Reload although the deletion was already committed.
resolution.correction: Allow bounded admission retry in the observing window during the existing detail-to-list transition and reuse the read request identity.
resolution.prevention: The real two-window regression verifies a single revision-5 deletion, retryable 429 followed by 200 on the same read, explicit refusals and exhausted contention.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard changes requested on b97fb772e969b93d2ddffbfcf84d4caa5fccc6b0. Original response SHA-256 5d8d2068e5e7f17d85a290457399b336c8897d7f8acc31a1386bf66fba0c58ce. The retained review and provenance are at archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m2-040-b97fb772.
items.observation: The candidate observer received a retryable HTTP 429 and retried the same note-list request. Holding its admitted reply left the client pending at 16.136 seconds. The drawer stayed on Loading, disabled close, and offered no Reload. Releasing that reply completed the read. This controlled delivery failure is separate from the original revision-5 contention diagnostic.

resolution.cause: A bounded admission loop still awaited an admitted reply indefinitely, leaving the observing drawer loading.
resolution.correction: Share one cancellable five-second deadline across the fallback snapshot and list, and discard late replies when the drawer closes or the selected note changes.
resolution.prevention: The desktop tests withhold the reply, check the timeout, Reload and Close, then deliver a stale 200 after a new selection and verify the selected note remains visible.

items.source: Guarded Windows task 45686354121 at 11a3ed67e9c5b95a98652c69731c13b35016b23c. Original report archives/runs/20261125T193505.526706Z-27a6ee5c/test-report.json and workspace reporter SHA-256 1678fc2e5ca32ddb399dfc0e67c275be749e1d484c0757db1438067c4489e40a. The unchanged extracted observation is archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/m2-040-windows-first-11a3ed67/original-observation.json (SHA-256 ee8c20dc513b80df9e3c3d70321835b49023f7179b954704b7acf9b3c776d869).
items.observation: The ordinary paired-window contention case failed at 16.153 seconds. The initiating window committed one deletion at revision 5 and its same-request list read went from 429 to 200. The observer's deleted detail returned HTTP 200 with DATA_UNAVAILABLE. Its next workspace snapshot received definite pre-admission HTTP 429 BUSY at 10598.476 milliseconds. It issued no snapshot retry or fallback note-list request and remained on Reload. This is a different read phase from the earlier list contention and held-reply findings.

resolution.cause: The observer retried the fallback list but abandoned the preceding snapshot when the writer temporarily refused admission. It could therefore stop before issuing a list read.
resolution.correction: Let the snapshot and the subsequent list recover explicit read-admission refusals within the same cancellable deadline. Terminal application replies still end their read.
resolution.prevention: On Linux and Windows the real paired-window journey first refuses the snapshot and then the list, recovers the same list request, shows both lists and verifies one deletion at revision 5. A separately admitted BUSY is terminal.

items.source: Ordinary PR124 run 45692536863 attempt 1. Complete artifacts at archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/pr124-native-original-45692536863/manifest.json, SHA-256 c246b0c5d27e69d2dfe540a7ddd634dfdd514c7eee9dbab33dbeabbb11da8c45. items.observation: The Windows core runner failed windows_venv_reaps_owned_leaf_before_recovery after the shared five-second witness at local_import.rs:1006 did not yield a complete interpreter PID, parent and environment. The worker-host library ran 28 tests and reported one failure. Both the historical launcher control and the directly owned child use that witness. The original leaves the failing call and child state unidentified. The same test passed in the earlier PR124 preview, the ordinary PR125 preview and protected main with matching worker test source. A local trusted-child exercise reproduced the same old timeout for an actual exit, a live silent child and a live partial record. No original Windows stage can be inferred from those controls.

resolution.cause: The two native interpreter checks shared an elapsed-time assertion which discarded the caller, protocol phase and partial-output state. The original timeout does not identify its runtime cause.
resolution.correction: The test checks the launcher and direct interpreter separately, reports the reached stage and validates the expected parent identity, locked Python environment and owned cleanup within the existing deadline.
resolution.prevention: The normal Rust suite checks exit, silent and partial responses. The Windows case verifies both caller identities, their package and path equivalence and teardown. Retained raw observations cover the original failure, earlier passing controls and the corrected non-elevated run.

items.observation: On protected main, desktop-localization timed out after 900.733 seconds. Well after the run finished, seven shell, pnpm and Vite processes still carried its exact SCOPEHUB_RUN_DIR and private temporary path across several sessions. The Vite process still held 127.0.0.1:1472. The cleanup failure is distinct from the cause of the original timeouts.

resolution.cause: A timed-out browser launcher could leave descendants that had created a separate session outside its process group.
resolution.correction: Supervise the Linux browser check with its own subreaper, then reap its descendants before returning the check result.
resolution.prevention: Exercise a detached listener and an unrelated live listener through the normal verification entry on exit, failure, timeout and interruption.

items.source: Astra Standard t10k on e11cec5729848235ed7ce066cd20402896b7cb7d. Original: archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m0-138-e11cec57/final-response.txt (SHA-256 0d20eb5a39cd0e72a2fa04638febb9c20a40a87646159b90b877b9ba054056c4).
items.observation: On the reviewed source a check command exited zero and its supervisor failed to read the owned children after a test-only descriptor limit. The harness returned cleanup_failed under default SIGCHLD. With SIGCHLD ignored it returned passed and zero for desktop-localization and market-recovery while the detached fixture still held its lock.

resolution.cause: An inherited ignored SIGCHLD disposition allowed a synthetic zero wait status when cleanup confirmation was missing.
resolution.correction: Require the supervisor to confirm its bounded cleanup through its result channel before accepting the command outcome.
resolution.prevention: The ordinary Linux tests exercise confirmed cleanup and an unavailable child inventory under default and ignored SIGCHLD dispositions.

items.source: Astra Standard t10k on e11cec5729848235ed7ce066cd20402896b7cb7d. Original: archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m0-138-e11cec57/final-response.txt (SHA-256 0d20eb5a39cd0e72a2fa04638febb9c20a40a87646159b90b877b9ba054056c4).
items.observation: One real SIGINT reached the serial check caller after its supervisor started reaping an owned detached tree. The reviewed desktop-localization and market-recovery entries escaped with KeyboardInterrupt and produced no interrupted check record. Independent cleanup confirmed the fixture processes exited.

resolution.cause: An interrupt arriving after the command result could escape while the supervisor was still waiting for descendants.
resolution.correction: Record the interrupt and complete bounded reaping before publishing the interrupted result.
resolution.prevention: A live supervisor and detached process exercise interruption during reaping and preserve the terminal row and subsequent retry.

items.source: Astra Standard t10k on 771d2071eff1b9215df7808cf1f51a9897334f07. Original text: archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m0-138-771d2071/final-response.txt (SHA-256 07417c896fa8f2810ee7644e12d106547cd766e263ae7b2b39b7f9f64ee7ead8). Original assistant response JSONL SHA-256 33a5a4a32d39546ef5af753e7fdbe86c06872bb036284f871d90cc7ee07c1378.
items.observation: An owned detached descendant kept an inherited stdout handle after a disposable supervisor hit EMFILE. The check correctly reported cleanup_failed. The descendant then appended 34 bytes after execute returned, invalidating the recorded SHA-256 under both tested SIGCHLD dispositions. The retry used its own log and did not restore integrity of the failed report.

resolution.cause: A surviving writer retained the original log descriptor after cleanup failed, allowing the digested log bytes to change later.
resolution.correction: Publish a bounded independent snapshot before computing the log digest when Linux cleanup is unconfirmed.
resolution.prevention: Retain the failed cleanup and allow the original writer to append after publication, then verify the archived bytes and a separate retry.

Original text: archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m0-138-771d2071/final-response.txt (SHA-256 07417c896fa8f2810ee7644e12d106547cd766e263ae7b2b39b7f9f64ee7ead8). Original assistant response JSONL SHA-256 33a5a4a32d39546ef5af753e7fdbe86c06872bb036284f871d90cc7ee07c1378.
items.observation: One standard SIGINT reached the serial caller while hashing a 16 MiB check log after normal command exit and confirmed cleanup. KeyboardInterrupt escaped with only the running row. The same observation was reproduced on the reviewed protected main ae479debd911ae79ffbf74f6208b288f00710978. This occurs without a residual output writer or an unconfirmed cleanup.

resolution.cause: A signal delivered during serial diagnostic finalization could escape before the harness saved a terminal result.
resolution.correction: Defer the interrupt across finalization and report its disposition while preserving an earlier cleanup failure.
resolution.prevention: Interrupt a real log digest and resolve the original terminal report, its latest copy and the independent retry.

items.source: Astra Standard t10k on 325b32e48b03c034f6080dc53909b9cf3e8e5944. Original: archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m0-138-325b32e4/final-response.txt (SHA-256 f6984eb538dcf7d69ffb19894ddd6beb6f4ae5265dc17605a1bb5bc29d57c288). Original event SHA-256 099069354f40cdbbbc1dcc56a6b23c7468db5ad1a6767444df451fff89c225e8.
items.observation: After the check had completed and its log had been hashed, a single SIGINT delivered while the terminal result write was blocked on a full 4 KiB stdout pipe left only the running row. The run report was absent and the latest report still referenced the preceding pass. The protected parent e2fc0a995de65253264e26c6d07f9adf9f9c2949 reproduced this boundary. The separate log-snapshot and digest-time interruption controls passed on the reviewed candidate.

resolution.cause: A blocked terminal-result write could receive the interrupt before the durable report was published.
resolution.correction: Make terminal output interruption observable and finish publishing the recorded check state and log.
resolution.prevention: Hold a real output pipe full, deliver one interrupt before drainage and independently verify the saved report and retry.

items.source: Astra Standard t10k on 5b968c9a96ea385a5efcb675ec7086d454574ecf. Original: archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m0-138-5b968c9a/final-response.txt (SHA-256 0843eda2c110a31aa8d8ad8fc8a2fd4cf6c31c1c338a802ccf502598f321398f). Original event SHA-256 968182378b3727933e75b541f4a49267afbd6c39924079119d6a1bf175e2bce3.
items.observation: A second writer filled the same Linux 4 KiB pipe after the parallel console poll reported write readiness and before os.write. One SIGINT set the cooperative stop flag, but the blocking write remained stuck after 5.5 seconds and neither the original report nor the new latest was published until external drainage. Filling before readiness retained the report without drainage. The independent sequential interruption, reaping and immutable-log controls passed.

resolution.cause: Another writer could fill the shared pipe after a readiness notification, leaving the ensuing blocking write stuck.
resolution.correction: Use a private nonblocking Linux file description and keep track of the unwritten bytes across short writes and EAGAIN.
resolution.prevention: Exercise pre-readiness and post-readiness fills, an undrained interrupt, actual short writes, unchanged caller flags and a complete byte-for-byte output line.

items.source: Guarded native M0-138 run 45682823289 attempt 1 and ordinary PR 124 run 45682766074 attempt 1. Original reports and traces are retained at archives/runs/20261125T191335.690626Z-3716de15/ and archives/runs/windows-change-45682766074-1/.
items.observation: Both Windows Python checks independently recorded two errors in test_windows_gated_launcher_is_the_assigned_process, in the redirector and normal gate subtests. The test replaces processes.sys with a namespace missing platform, and containment selection reads that property before either launcher starts. The logs therefore contain no native gate process identity or Job Object membership result for either subtest. Guarded Linux passed and the ordinary Linux Python check passed. Its aggregate retains its recorded blocked status.

resolution.cause: The interpreter-path fixture replaced the process module’s runtime namespace with a stub lacking the platform read by process containment before launch. Both the redirector and normal case errored before checking identity.
resolution.correction: Preserve the actual runtime platform in the two controlled interpreter configurations and let the existing gate-launch test exercise its process identity and containment assertions.
resolution.prevention: Run the assigned-process test on Windows alongside its redirector control, the timeout cleanup and the external reader. The Linux contrast independently checks a distinct redirector PID and process group.

items.source: Protected Linux run 45712964544 and identical-tree PR 124 run 45709305124. Original report archives/runs/20261125T222514.810400Z-4ec1e5c9/test-report.json. The retained comparison is archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/m0-157-terminal-lock-45712964544/observation.json (SHA-256 b3cecaac05b7015850f94c1fd80de73cacbc09b2b066d49572024e8eaff45d23). Linux PR 128 run 45716055348 attempt 1 repeated the failure. Original report archives/runs/20261125T224715.532164Z-bac3bdc0/test-report.json. The retained source comparison is archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/m0-157-pull-request-recurrence-45716055348/observation.json (SHA-256 08b406ade058259e18b01270e84943b3cfae607b7ae16277e92f352fb8b15187).
items.observation: The final running-stage subtest acquired the peer lock after one SIGINT. Its seven-scenario test took 30.242 seconds and the helper uses a 30-second lifetime starting before the scenarios. The same-tree PR completed the test in 16.462 seconds. The failing run did not report the helper exit reason or lock-release time. PR 128 hit the identical final running-stage assertion in 30.851 seconds, the sole failure among 838 tests. The protected, submitted and preview sources match on the five involved code paths. The second hosted report also lacks peer exit and lock-release telemetry.

resolution.cause: The test peer had a 30-second independent lifetime. A controlled slow run observed it exiting normally and releasing the lock before the final stage. The original hosted runs did not record the exit reason.
resolution.correction: The test controller owns the stdin writer and the independent peer holds the lock until EOF. Cleanup reaps the peer and verifies release.
resolution.prevention: The seven-stage public SIGINT test checks that the unrelated peer keeps its lock and that reports, cleanup and retries remain intact. Retained controls verify the old deadline, deliberate early release and controller exit.

items.source: PR 116 ordinary native Windows run 45682874140 on 00dfb23fc59e5e73f964eb574d29edfb48c5bf5e. Original archives/runs/windows-change-45682874140-1/test-report.json and workspace-timeframe.log. The corresponding native Linux check passed. Protected Windows run 45702463807 and same-tree preview run 45698603142: archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/main-python-and-indicator-45702463807/observations.json SHA-256 31ae8c90aff05cae6779e17f0603ac4fe4431e00ff6adefcb02372146d669ae9.
items.observation: After the first ready status for task 479d7460-afa8-421a-b8bd-34759939826d was reset, status cadf2bd2 received HTTP 429 BUSY and 5175c3ec reached another ready reply whose delivery was reset. The expected terminal message and a cancellation were observed with no new preview submission. The assertion expected one raw status request and rejected both outbound reads. A local Chromium replay with the portable writer reproduced the false count using a real authenticated refusal. When a separate control substituted HTTP 200 BUSY for an admitted ready response, the preview retried and displayed the result. An application BUSY does not establish that a request was refused before admission. The protected failure in the full or cropped zero-volatility case printed two different status request IDs for the same synthetic task. Those HTTP outcomes were not observed. Its preceding preview with the identical Git tree passed the named case.

resolution.cause: The recovery assertion counted every outgoing status request as an admitted read. Polling also treated an admitted application BUSY as a refusal. The protected equal-closes failure did not retain the HTTP outcomes of its two reads.
resolution.correction: Classify a retry from the documented admission response, keep polling the original frozen task within one deadline and account for each attempted status and cancellation.
resolution.prevention: Exercise full and cropped zero-volatility calculations, zero through two lost ready replies, a contradictory or nonretryable 429, admitted BUSY, persistent refusal and wrong-task replies in the real workspace.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard review of 2738fa7edc800b37ba3eb3d4196eb86908e36104. Private original independent-final-m0-149-2738fa7e/final-response.txt SHA-256 a3408ef80cae92a7bba28f669213a0bc8ea0e51f53ddd66b529ce6863a5146a7.
items.observation: The native polling replay reads the same task again after an admitted retryable BUSY. Tauri treats all retryable BUSY replies as refusals even though reaching a ready indicator job can acquire the writer slot and return SQLite BUSY during its application read.

resolution.cause: The native transport treated every retryable BUSY as a refusal even when the application had admitted the read and SQLite returned BUSY.
resolution.correction: The writer marks refused admission in the native error details only before admission. Native polling retries a matching, explicitly refused status read.
resolution.prevention: A built desktop transport exercises explicit writer refusal, an admitted storage BUSY, an older unclassified reply and the nonretryable shape. The latter three each produce one read and one same-task cancellation.

items.observation: Adding a raw task.cancel without task_id and with HTTP 400 to the retained cut=0 browser journal passes the recorded verifier. There is no previous task in this trial, but the missing task is classified as previous cleanup and skipped.

resolution.cause: The first trial treated a missing cancellation identity as a match for its absent previous task.
resolution.correction: Match cancellation against an actual current or prior task identity and count cleanup independently for each trial.
resolution.prevention: The retained full and cropped trial sequence accepts identified prior-task cleanup, rejects an added first-trial cancellation without a task and verifies one cancellation on exhaustion.

items.observation: After an upstream HTTP 200 ready status for the frozen task was reset at 349 ms, the persistent-refusal test saw a different request for the same task at 15247 ms on its explicit synthetic route. Chromium recorded net::ERR_ABORTED with no HTTP status or reply. The journal assertion counted that unresolved request alongside the real ready observation and failed the Linux case. The abort does not identify an admitted read or a delivered refusal. The matching Windows case passed. The failed assertion retained a printed subset and no complete bounded journal attachment.

resolution.cause: The original persistent-refusal browser assertion classified an aborted terminal request with no HTTP result alongside admitted recovery. Its failure retained a partial journal, leaving the original request disposition unclassified.
resolution.correction: Record the browser deadline, held test route and delivery outcome together and require proof the terminal request was never forwarded before accepting this bounded abort.
resolution.prevention: Exercise the held browser route and check two delivered refusals, a single terminal abort, no new status or preview after the deadline and one cancellation of the original task. Reject incomplete or contradictory journals.

items.source: Protected main push 45668943982, attempt 1, Windows browser producer 139398629052. The aggregate report is archives/runs/windows-change-45668943982-1/test-report.json. Its workspace-timeframe log has SHA-256 79d9d51be67b34df9c44be45c536f233d9eb17ac5a4e642c6d6eddcade96a35c.
items.observation: The test-owned private handoff verifier reported subprocess deadline exceeded during its first assertion. Of 76 native Windows workspace cases, 73 passed and two used their documented platform skips. All 64 isolated workspace profiles prepared in 138 ms. The descriptor verdict and last internal stage were not observed. The earlier M0-125 incident had no classified subprocess outcome.

resolution.cause: The original protected Windows log classifies deadline expiry at the first handoff assertion. The cause, last internal stage and descriptor verdict remain unknown.
resolution.correction: Use the existing test-owned bounded launcher with the native Rust file witness for the real handoff. The witness reads ownership, inherited and effective rights, and verifies an actual read/write open under the existing ten-second limit.
resolution.prevention: The first live case passed on Windows in ordinary PR run 45769667627 and guarded run 45769688721 with the original descriptor refusals, cleanup and capability rotation. Separate child controls cover deadline classification and reaping. The coordinator owns verification of the first protected main push after integration.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard t10c at 0ff1c4da15fbede912b909aef2ad226ba7fce838. Archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m0-147-0ff1c4da/final-response.txt SHA-256 9f8962801f6995ffc670ea32d8c58775dd127cb1f9ab0f4a63418c6518d2df7d; original response line SHA-256 7424ed9411eca2881653faadab3e0319e63222f00baf0483d801a67d2c670c1e.
items.observation: The raw native handoff checker classifies every access-allowed entry before asking whether it grants access to this regular file. A valid private handoff with an inherited effective user grant and a zero-mask or inherit-only allow for another trustee can therefore receive exit 58. The earlier Framework file access-control view removes both entries during leaf ACL normalization. The independent finding is a source observation and does not explain the original subprocess deadline.

resolution.cause: The witness evaluated trustee identity before applying the regular-file filter for zero-mask and inherit-only allow entries.
resolution.correction: Validate the entry layout and apply the legacy leaf filter before evaluating the trustee of a surviving grant.
resolution.prevention: The mandatory native file matrix in runs 45769667627 and 45769688721 passed zero-mask and inherit-only allow cases and retained exit 58 for an effective grant to another trustee. Independent review confirmed that each row passes exact readback, legacy managed and Rust witness assertions.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard t10c at a5b94b98ab0ed7446787dfbee899c63cc731d2a2. Archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m0-147-a5b94b98/final-response.txt SHA-256 ccc7058df47dfc3c8f22ca01d8ec4854e658952de6a51c3f844aa35bfeb1d0be; original response line SHA-256 a00f5e9e6148b308c5172ad8dc57cbace827d2eb35d8a12a6838fcd23fb27290.
items.observation: The independent handoff witness returns 54 for a callback allow by type before checking its mask or applicability. The retained native regular-file matrix shows that the previous managed leaf projection drops structurally valid zero-mask and inherit-only callbacks. An effective callback remains unsupported. The current result does not explain the original subprocess deadline.

resolution.cause: Dispatch by unsupported ACE type preceded layout and leaf applicability checks, so inert callback grants could be refused before the legacy leaf exclusion.
resolution.correction: Validate known callback and object layouts before filtering inert entries and reject an effective unsupported grant.
resolution.prevention: The native matrix in runs 45769667627 and 45769688721 passed the inert callback and object rows and required exit 54 for each effective unsupported row. The separately executed Rust parser suite rejects malformed and oversized entries before filtering.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard review of 7f12b10735fbe092a2a86cdbb58d4b31d1a797a6. Original at archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m0-147-7f12b107/original-assistant-response.jsonl (SHA-256 f73948ec6631ca5509b82863a5afa5b7553a9fe532881f55d08d5a0ae6fc3b9a). items.observation: The guarded M0-147 task selects environment, project state, Python and workspace checks. The Windows workspace setup builds windows_handoff_probe without running its seven portable Rust tests. The task can consequently pass without evidence for malformed entry rejection even when the example builds and native file comparisons run.

resolution.cause: The task selected the browser harness that built the example but omitted the existing Rust workspace check that executes its parser tests.
resolution.correction: Select rust-contracts-workers as a required M0-147 check and register the maintained example as a Cargo test target.
resolution.prevention: The guarded Linux and Windows originals from run 45769688721 each list seven windows_handoff_probe tests passed, including malformed and oversized entry controls. The separate Windows workspace-timeframe result covers the mandatory 24 regular-file comparisons.

In the independent combined control, the row 19 ACL revision readback diagnosis was replaced by row 0 cleanup EPERM with an absolute fixture path. The 24 expected ACL outcomes, bounded marker vocabulary and native deadline were independently preserved.

See archives/runs/windows-change-45710866374-1/test-report.json and archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/m0-147-native-first-row-45710866374/observation.json (SHA-256 f26fea324bf7b3ec08d3b6dd369915963f6acd68cf07f242ded6032b573cc845). See archives/runs/20261125T221246.075646Z-9b2ba873/test-report.json and archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/m0-147-native-first-row-45710987464/observation.json (SHA-256 d6fd07520520dd30a6cbdd027a4b672a99c36a2c1a327942c5a44ad8b01b1f4f). items.observation: Both Windows reports recorded 89 workspace cases passed, two skipped, one failed and zero flaky. The workspace journey passed the first live handoff and its two unsuitable descriptor controls plus the read-only control before matrix preparation reported no stored fixture trustee ACE for allow-zero-mask. No matrix witness result or subsequent capability rotation was reached. The guarded Linux task passed all five checks. Both native Rust suites separately passed protected regular-file zero-mask storage with an explicit owner grant. The first-row report did not measure the submitted ACE or a second reader. The cause of the earlier deadline and the row in earlier generic readback failures remain unknown. In the subsequent native calibration the two readers disagreed about the inherited grant even on the untouched baseline. All six proposed writes returned input-error before the write call. The witnesses saw the original files. No proposed writer was qualified by this experiment.

resolution.cause: The original first-row failures observed no fixture trustee ACE through one reader and did not observe the submitted bytes. Calibration found reader disagreement on the untouched baseline, and six proposed writes stopped before submission. The cause of the original missing row remains unknown.
resolution.correction: Use the protected test fixture writer with agreeing named and handle baselines. Verify exact submitted and stored ACEs, ACL revision and preservation of the inherited grant before comparing the managed and native witness results.
resolution.prevention: Run 45748342112 directly observed two qualifying writes and managed and Rust outcomes 0 and 58. The independently reviewed mandatory 24-row loop passed in ordinary Windows run 45769667627 and guarded Windows run 45769688721.

items.source: Independent Astra Standard review of bc89c85dcaf81f359c91adc23e7c87fa08a70966 at archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/independent-final-m0-147-bc89c85d/final-response.txt (SHA-256 38109616760dc41d7be3eafe91b0a3de4051f9c5c5bd467704223c1eb676e09a). Local Node 24.22.3 reproduction at 3620427e1f9ca51cf1aaac8a629f067ca75659e6 in .reports/m0-147-first-row/portable-baseline.log (SHA-256 c7dc86bf7f0838a4036d3ea223fbcec8d88a439e395583e6f5278a1c016e0037).
items.observation: The real portable calibration child returned exit 4 but the parser reported an unavailable diagnostic for a valid stderr marker. With execFile in the local checkout, Node stream writes returned no stdout or stderr bytes with either forced or natural exit. Synchronous writes returned five decoy stdout bytes and all 38 marker stderr bytes. The independent positive and rejected handoff child controls and the combined cleanup failure passed. Both latest hosted Windows runs passed the portable diagnostic cases. This observation concerns the portable child transport.

resolution.cause: The real portable child produced no captured bytes through Node stream writes in the observed local execFile control, including natural exit.
resolution.correction: Write the synthetic control streams synchronously and keep stderr as the diagnostic marker source.
resolution.prevention: The real-child control asserts the exact bounded row and field for stderr, fixed fallback for a stdout-only lookalike, cleanup of all acquired fixtures and no witness launch after failed preparation. Independent review replayed both cases and guarded workspace-timeframe passed on Linux and Windows.

items.source: Observed on ff6c880b289b18e3e58d667dcb5b76c7f12fe053. archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/coordinator-checkpoints/resume-t113-20261126T0228Z/rule-effects-main-ff6c880b.json (SHA-256 10c6688525ca8763b09a223b721970b87a0ff84e914100475a684b1826a7a764).
items.observation: The fixed UI-last instruction in repository_layout.implementation_instructions coexists with a policy to test the highest uncertainty first. The root guide also directs future shared-capability work to a parent ai-cap rule without a source in the protected checkout or its applicable instruction ancestors. The chart false-positive is independent evidence for the importance of testing the user-visible boundary. Its cause has not been attributed to the wording.

resolution.cause: The repository layout directed contributors to leave UI until last while delivery prescribed the first observable high-risk boundary. The parent-rule reference had no usable source in a clean checkout.
resolution.correction: Root and layout guidance now resolve to the versioned first-test and dependency rules, including a chart distinction, a protocol boundary and the appropriate local or provider requirements.
resolution.prevention: Focused checks resolve the portable references and their source rules. Independent review exercised normal navigation, a rejected pointer, and valid and oversized frames.

items.source: Protected Windows main run 45709117560, first attempt, and the same-tree first ordinary PR 129 run 45705520154. The authenticated recovery producer, original chart screenshot and both test reporters are indexed in archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/m0-154-cold-sample-45709117560/observations.json (SHA-256 73542c6956547a0746dad8eba3bed2f2b2b599f6b38d4c78ae379b00b0957736). items.observation: The first closed-bar repair browser case stopped at the ten-second DOMContentLoaded deadline. Its retained screenshot shows the static Opening ScopeHub panel and the manual reload control. Eleven other recovery cases passed. The same-tree ordinary Windows PR passed all twelve cases, including the original case in 5.549 seconds. The failed trace does not identify the document response stage or timing of individual module loads. It contains no failing chart repair assertion.

resolution.cause: The former DOMContentLoaded wait stopped before chart assertions and did not report document or asset milestones. The precise trigger for the historical Windows timeout remains unknown.
resolution.correction: Observe the public sample navigation and report a failed document, a committed document with pending code, or verified catalog, history and chart milestones. Keep the 10,000 ms navigation deadline and manual reload.
resolution.prevention: The first ordinary Windows run 45823554677 verified the cold repair sample at 2,154 ms. The held required module stayed document-committed at 10,011 ms against an independent 10,012 ms reading. The failed-document and held dynamic entry controls also passed.

Shifting the history start by one minute, changing the catalog limit from 50 to 49 or reversing the two requests each made the startup entry reject, but the attachment reported history-verified in every rejected case.

resolution.cause: The witness credited successful replies before validating the exact outgoing requests and their order.

resolution.prevention: The market-recovery controls now stop at catalog-verified for a shifted history start and at dom-content-loaded for a changed catalog limit or reversed requests.

items.observation: The real held-module attachment recorded 10,018 ms. The retained observation qualifier accepted copies reporting 0 ms and 60,000 ms, while rejecting a wrong pending script path. The browser check asserted the ten-second timeout text, stage and script path without checking attachment elapsed time.

resolution.cause: The original held-module check validated the timeout text, stage and asset without checking the reported elapsed time.
resolution.correction: Qualify elapsed time against the existing 10,000 ms deadline and an independent monotonic clock reading.
resolution.prevention: The held-module case retains both readings and rejects copied observations of 0 and 60,000 ms. The Windows first-attempt values were 10,011 and 10,012 ms.

The startup attachment nevertheless recorded history_verified_ms and history-verified before the chart visibility assertion failed.

resolution.cause: The witness compared fewer response fields than the application and accepted a snapshot with shifted bounds for the correct request.
resolution.correction: Use the shared request-bound history checks for the application and startup witness before crediting the frozen sample.
resolution.prevention: The public startup case pairs the ordinary history control with the schema-valid shifted snapshot. The shifted reply stops at catalog-verified with a validation alert and zero chart bars.

items.source: Independent changes-requested decision 25f18c909377b012f42761502c36a36bb32c99dd46f8b4539cce6c9a2a39d98b for source 2f02d0f7d674bf1fb83b507f1e3303f3a7edaad5. items.observation: Removing only the required snapshot.content_hash from the matched 40-bar success reply still rendered all 40 bars in Chromium and produced sample-verified when the recorded events were replayed through the startup observer. Existing browser cases removed a field the request comparison already checked, omitted the whole result, shifted the range or changed event order. They did not reject a schema-invalid success that passed the shared comparisons. The first-page check compared the absent hash with itself and treated equality as proof of identity.

resolution.cause: Both consumers trusted the runtime shape of the decoded reply, and equality of two missing hash fields passed the identity comparison.
resolution.correction: Require generated operation output validation before the application and the startup witness admit catalog or history data.
resolution.prevention: The public startup controls admit compatible history and reject missing or malformed content hashes, other structural omissions and a legacy bars reply supplied as frozen history.
